title: No NaN/Infinity/bounds validation on parsed GPX lat/lon/ele; malformed coordinates silently corrupt the entire plan
verdictReason: Re-opened gpx.ts:43-47: `return points.map((pt) => ({ lat: Number(pt['@_lat']), lon: Number(pt['@_lon']), ele: Number(pt['ele']) }))` has zero Number.isFinite/bounds guard. Empirically confirmed Number(undefined)=NaN, Number('abc')=NaN, Number('1e999')=Infinity. Traced NaN propagation: haversine (geo.ts:18-28) returns NaN for NaN coords (verified by running the actual formula), and buildMicroSegments (gpx.ts:128) feeds that into distance_m, cum_distance_m and the grade computation with no guard, so a single non-numeric trkpt silently NaN-poisons the whole solver output. The asymmetry the candidate flags is real: api/handler.ts:52-53 does exactly `if (!Number.isFinite(lat) || !Number.isFinite(lon)) return null;` plus the [-90,90]/[-180,180] bounds check the GPX path omits. Severity high is justified as a data-integrity defect (a wrong race plan presented as valid); note this is a local/single-user tool so it is a robustness/correctness issue rather than a remote exploit.
evidence: gpx.ts:43-47 `lat: Number(pt['@_lat']), lon: Number(pt['@_lon']), ele: Number(pt['ele'])` with no finite/bounds check; geo.ts haversine returns NaN for NaN input (verified by re-running the formula); api/handler.ts:52-53 already does the matching Number.isFinite+bounds validation on the network path.
recommendation: After Number() conversion, reject the point or throw a typed ParseError unless Number.isFinite(lat) && Number.isFinite(lon) && lat in [-90,90] && lon in [-180,180]; default ele to 0 when non-finite. Mirror the existing api/handler.ts:52-53 validation so the file-upload path matches the network path.

title: parseGpxString throws unhandled TypeError on any non-GPX or structurally-malformed XML (no null guards on gpx/trk/trkseg)
verdictReason: Primary claim confirmed at gpx.ts:20-37: `const gpx = doc['gpx'] as Record<string, unknown>` then unchecked `gpx['trk']`/`trkObj['trkseg']` casts. Empirically reproduced the exact errors: '<root/>' -> "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trk')", '<gpx></gpx>' -> "...reading 'trkseg'", plaintext and JSON also throw a raw TypeError. The web App.tsx path is correctly described (try/catch spans lines 65-89 with ingestGpxString at line 77, degrading to fetchStatus 'error'). ADJUSTED because two secondary line citations are wrong: the worker pipeline calls ingestGpxString at apps/web/src/lib/pipeline.ts:170 (the cited :126 is the unrelated controlsFromStops function), and the CLI cites fileIo.ts:35,42 which is correct. runPipeline (pipeline.ts:144-170) has no local try/catch, confirming the worker surfaces a raw stack trace. Severity medium is fair: only a robustness/UX defect (opaque error vs typed message) on a local tool, not an availability attack.
evidence: gpx.ts:20 `const gpx = doc['gpx'] as Record<string, unknown>`; gpx.ts:30/37 unchecked trkseg/trkpt access; reproduced TypeErrors for <root/>, <gpx></gpx>, plaintext, JSON. Unguarded ingest call is at apps/web/src/lib/pipeline.ts:170 (candidate said 126).
recommendation: Validate each level (gpx, trk, trkseg, trkpt) and throw a single descriptive/typed error such as 'not a valid GPX file' instead of a raw TypeError, so the CLI and worker pipeline (pipeline.ts:170) surface a clear message.

title: No file-size or point-count cap before GPX parse — unbounded memory on large or maliciously crafted input
verdictReason: Confirmed there is no byte cap or point-count cap: parseGpxString parses the full XML and points.map materializes every trkpt unbounded (gpx.ts:43), and dedupePoints/smoothElevation are O(n) passes over all points. A grep for file.size/byteLength/MAX_*SIZE/length-caps across UploadForm.tsx, fileIo.ts and ingest/ returned nothing. ADJUSTED on two counts: (1) the cited entry-point line numbers are wrong - `await file.text()` is at UploadForm.tsx:183 (not :130) and `readFileSync(path, 'utf8')` is at fileIo.ts:43 (parseGpx is :36; the candidate's :35 is the function signature line); (2) severity lowered medium->low because this is a privacy-first local/browser tool with no server-side parsing of attacker-controlled uploads (the comment in UploadForm.tsx:8 and App privacy note confirm nothing is uploaded). The only victim of a giant GPX is the user's own browser tab/CLI process, so impact is self-inflicted resource exhaustion, not a multi-user DoS.
evidence: gpx.ts:43 unbounded points.map; UploadForm.tsx:183 `const text = await file.text();` with no file.size check; fileIo.ts:43 readFileSync(path,'utf8'); grep found no existing size/count caps anywhere in the ingest paths.
recommendation: Optionally enforce a byte cap (check file.size in onGpxChange before file.text(), and buffer length in the CLI) and a parsed point-count cap. Low priority given the local-only trust model.

title: GPX XML parser config is safe against XXE and DOCTYPE entity-expansion (billion laughs) under fast-xml-parser v5.8.0
verdictReason: Verified gpx.ts:14-17 constructs `new XMLParser({ ignoreAttributes: false, attributeNamePrefix: '@_' })` with no entity options. Empirically with the installed fast-xml-parser 5.8.0 (package.json declares '^5.8.0', node_modules resolves to 5.8.0): a SYSTEM 'file:///etc/passwd' external entity throws "External entities are not supported", and a nested DOCTYPE billion-laughs entity (&lol3;) is returned literally (output length 43, the entity string '&lol3;' preserved un-expanded) so no amplification occurs. This is an accurate positive/info finding. The '^5.8.0' caret does allow future 5.x defaults to drift, so the pinning recommendation is sound.
evidence: gpx.ts:14-17 XMLParser options carry no processEntities override; runtime test on installed 5.8.0: external-entity parse throws 'External entities are not supported', billion-laughs &lol3; returns literal (len 43, not expanded). package.json:15 declares fast-xml-parser '^5.8.0'; installed version 5.8.0.
recommendation: No change required for the current XXE/entity-expansion posture. Consider an upper bound on the fast-xml-parser version and an explicit DOCTYPE/processEntities option to make the safety explicit and resistant to a future dependency-default change.

title: FIT binary ingest copies the entire untrusted file via Array.from(bytes) with no size cap
verdictReason: Verified fit.ts:15 `const stream = Stream.fromByteArray(Array.from(bytes));` converts the whole Uint8Array to a JS number[] before decoding with no length cap; empirically confirmed Array.from(new Uint8Array([...])) yields a real number[] (each element a JS number, so the boxed copy is substantially larger than the packed Uint8Array). Bytes come from untrusted uploads: the cited entry points exist, though one line number is off - `await file.arrayBuffer()` is at UploadForm.tsx:195 (candidate said :142) and readFileSync(path) is at fileIo.ts:54 (parseGpx/readFitPower region; candidate's :53 is the function signature). Severity low is appropriate and matches the candidate. Keeping verdict confirmed since the line-number drift is minor secondary-citation noise and does not change the finding; the core fit.ts:15 cite is exact.
evidence: fit.ts:15 `Stream.fromByteArray(Array.from(bytes))`; Array.from on a Uint8Array confirmed to produce a number[]; untrusted bytes from UploadForm.tsx:195 `await file.arrayBuffer()` and fileIo.ts:54 readFileSync(path).
recommendation: Cap FIT byte length before decoding (real activity files are well under a few MB) and wrap decode in a descriptive error so a malformed FIT does not propagate a raw exception to the CLI/worker.

title: CLI config and ensemble-cache JSON.parse use unchecked `as` casts but operate on local/trusted files
verdictReason: loadConfig.ts:14 confirmed exactly: `const raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8')) as RawConfig;` with no runtime schema validation (applyDefaults is called next but the 'as RawConfig' cast itself validates nothing). The localStorage parse cited as UploadForm.tsx:68 is actually at line 100 inside loadFromStorage, and it IS correctly guarded by try/catch (lines 97-103) as the candidate states. title: Unencrypted RSA private key written to temp dir is never deleted
verdictReason: Confirmed in substance, but the cited file path is wrong: `packages/cli/src/ciqCompile.ts` does not exist. The real file is `packages/cli/src/buildCiq.ts`. In `ensureDeveloperKey()` (lines 29-53): `const tmp = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'ciq-key-'))` (line 33), `execFileSync('openssl', ['genrsa', '-out', pem, '4096'], ...)` writes a 4096-bit RSA private key PEM to `k.pem` (line 35), then `openssl pkcs8 -nocrypt` derives the DER (lines 36-52). There is no rmSync/unlink/finally; the plaintext PEM persists in $TMPDIR after the function returns. mkdtemp dir is 0700 so exposure is limited to the local user. Severity low is correct. Adjusted file path and line range (78-87 -> 33-52).
evidence: buildCiq.ts:33 `const tmp = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'ciq-key-'));` line 35 `execFileSync('openssl', ['genrsa', '-out', pem, '4096'], { stdio: 'pipe' });` No cleanup of `tmp`/`pem` anywhere in the file (107 lines, verified).
recommendation: Wrap key generation so the temp PEM and its mkdtemp dir are removed in a `finally` (`fs.rmSync(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true })`). The mkdtemp dir is 0700 so exposure is limited to the local user, but a long-lived plaintext signing key in tmp is unnecessary residue.

title: race_date interpolated into cache filename without sanitization (path traversal)
verdictReason: Confirmed in substance. `cachePath` (cache.ts:38-40) does `return path.join(projectRoot(), '.cache', `weather-${raceDate}.json`)` with no sanitization, and the value flows into both `fs.writeFileSync` (writeCache, line 49) and `fs.readFileSync`+`JSON.parse` (readCache, lines 81-82). raceDate originates from `cfg.race_date`. No regex/format validation of race_date exists anywhere in core. A value like `../../tmp/x` would resolve outside `.cache/`. Local-trusted-config caveat and low severity are correct (runPlan is not reachable from web/api). Adjusted the config.ts line reference 54 -> 61.
evidence: cache.ts:39 `return path.join(projectRoot(), '.cache', `weather-${raceDate}.json`);`. config.ts:61 `if (!raw.race_date) throw new Error('Config is missing mandatory field: race_date');` (truthiness only, no format check).

Severity is low because config.json is a local, trusted input for this local CLI tool, but the unchecked interpolation into a write/read path is a latent traversal if the config source ever becomes untrusted.

verdictReason: Confirmed in substance, line numbers corrected. cache.ts is only 84 lines, so the cited 85-86 is out of range; the actual code is at lines 81-82: `const raw = fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf-8'); return JSON.parse(raw) as EnsembleField;` with an unchecked cast and no try/catch around JSON.parse (only the statSync at lines 66-70 is guarded). title: outDir / outPath are unvalidated and not confined to a base directory
verdictReason: Confirmed in substance, line cite corrected. cli.ts:108-109 `const outDir = opts.outDir ?? 'output'; mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });` (candidate cited 91-92; the actual code is at 108-109). outDir comes verbatim from `--out`/`--outDir` (parseArgs line 261) and is used to build write paths (tempokort.md, workout.fit, plan.json etc. via join, lines 181-186) and passed indirectly to writers. title: No rate limiting or auth on public weather endpoint enables upstream quota/cost DoS via fan-out amplification
verdictReason: Core claim holds. handleWeather (handler.ts:60-69) only calls parseWeatherQuery then gatherWindSamples with no auth/rate-limit gate. fetchAll.ts:80-85 confirms 1 batched forecast + 3*N per-point fetches (ensemble/smhi/met via mapLimit). MAX_POINTS=64 (handler.ts:32) => up to 1+3*64=193 upstream fetches per cache miss. vercel.json has no WAF/middleware and there is no middleware.ts in the repo. Adjusted: cited line 59-65 was imprecise (the gatherWindSamples call is line 69; handleWeather body is 60-69). Also CONCURRENCY=10 (fetchAll.ts:41) caps in-flight per-source fetches and the s-maxage=10800 CDN cache absorbs repeated identical requests, bounding sustained abuse. Severity high retained, scoped to cache-miss / cache-busting traffic.
evidence: handler.ts:69 `const samples = await gatherWindSamples(parsed.points, parsed.date);` with no auth/rate-limit. fetchAll.ts:80-85 Promise.all of fetchOpenMeteoForecastBatched + 3x mapLimit(points, CONCURRENCY=10). MAX_POINTS=64 => up to 193 upstream fetches/miss. vercel.json (6 lines) defines only build/output/install; grep for ratelimit/RateLimit returned nothing.
recommendation: Add per-IP rate limiting before the fan-out (Vercel WAF rule, Edge middleware, or KV token bucket) and an upstream concurrency/quota budget. Prioritize defenses against cache-busting callers since the CDN cache already absorbs identical repeated requests.

title: Date validated for format but not range; distinct dates/coords bust the s-maxage CDN cache and amplify upstream load
verdictReason: Confirmed. handler.ts:26 `const ISO_DATE = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/;` and handler.ts:42 `if (!date || !ISO_DATE.test(date) || !pts) return null;` validate only the YYYY-MM-DD shape, not range or calendar validity. The date is forwarded verbatim as start_date/end_date to upstreams (openMeteo.ts:54-55 buildEnsembleUrl, openMeteo.ts:116-118 buildForecastUrlMulti). Coordinates accept full precision (handler.ts:50-53 only checks finiteness + bounds, no rounding). weatherClient.ts:4-6 roundPt snaps to 0.1deg but is client-side only and an attacker hitting /api/weather directly bypasses it. Each unique (date,pts) tuple is a distinct CDN cache key forcing a full ~193-fetch fan-out.
evidence: handler.ts:26 ISO_DATE regex shape-only; handler.ts:42 tests shape only; handler.ts:50-53 coords validated for finiteness/bounds only, not rounded; openMeteo.ts:55 `start_date: date, end_date: date` forwards arbitrary valid-format date upstream. weatherClient.ts:4-6 roundPt is client-side only.
recommendation: Clamp date to a sane forward window (today..today+N days) and snap/round coordinates server-side to a cache-friendly grid (e.g. 0.1deg) before building upstream URLs, bounding cache keys and preventing unique-key amplification.

title: No timeout/abort on upstream fetch calls; a hanging provider ties up the serverless function for its full execution window
verdictReason: Confirmed. fetchAll.ts:45 `await fetch(buildSmhiUrl(point))`, fetchAll.ts:55 `await fetch(buildMetNorwayUrl(point), { headers: metNorwayHeaders() })`, fetchAll.ts:65 `await fetch(buildEnsembleUrl(point, date))` and openMeteo.ts:151 all call fetch with no signal/AbortController/timeout. grep for AbortController/AbortSignal/signal: across api/ and weather/ returned nothing. The try/catch catches rejection, not a hang, so a slow/hanging upstream blocks until the Vercel function timeout, and Promise.all joining all four source groups means one hang stalls the whole request.
evidence: fetchAll.ts:45,55,65 plain `await fetch(...)` with no signal; openMeteo.ts:151 same. grep for AbortController/AbortSignal/signal: in api/ + packages/core/src/weather/ returned no matches. catch blocks (fetchAll.ts:48-50) handle rejection but not a hang.
recommendation: Wrap each fetch with an AbortController + short per-fetch timeout (5-8s) so a dead source fails fast into the existing catch-and-return-[] path instead of holding the function open until the platform timeout.

title: No CORS headers set; acceptable for same-origin web app but undocumented and unenforced
verdictReason: Confirmed as informational / no-action. weather.ts:8 `for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(result.headers)) res.setHeader(k, v);` sets only the headers from handleWeather, which (handler.ts:73) are just Cache-Control and Content-Type. No Access-Control-Allow-Origin anywhere. weatherClient.ts:18-20 calls the endpoint same-origin. Absence of CORS is the correct default for same-origin-only access and the data is non-sensitive public weather, so this is purely a documentation note.
evidence: weather.ts:8-9 sets only result.headers; handler.ts:73 returns only Cache-Control + Content-Type; no ACAO header in repo; weatherClient.ts:19 fetches same-origin `/api/weather`.
recommendation: No security action needed. Optionally document that the missing CORS header is an intentional same-origin-only decision.

title: Upstream JSON parsed as `any` with no schema validation; malformed/hostile provider data can produce NaN values in response but is bounded
verdictReason: Confirmed at low severity. parseOpenMeteo (openMeteo.ts:71) takes `json: any` and indexes parallel arrays (openMeteo.ts:79-83) using times.length as loop bound (openMeteo.ts:86) without checking other arrays' lengths/finiteness. openMeteo.ts:94 `pressure_pa: pressures[i] * 100` yields NaN when pressures[i] is undefined; speeds[i]/dirs[i] (lines 91-92) likewise unvalidated. smhi.ts:32 and metNorway.ts:52 use the same `any` pattern (though they skip entries missing ws/wd). Upstreams are fixed trusted hosts so not an injection vector, and output bounded by MAX_POINTS, making this a graceful-degradation/robustness issue rather than a direct exploit. Low severity correct.
evidence: openMeteo.ts:76-83 destructures hourly arrays with `?? []`; openMeteo.ts:86 loops on times.length only; openMeteo.ts:91-94 push speeds[i]/dirs[i]/pressures[i]*100 with no finiteness/length-parity check. smhi.ts:32 `json?.timeSeries ?? []`; metNorway.ts:52-53 same `any` pattern.
recommendation: Validate numeric fields are finite (Number.isFinite) before pushing samples and confirm array length parity, so a truncated/malformed upstream response degrades gracefully instead of emitting NaN into the client-facing EnsembleField.

title: No SSRF: all upstream URLs use hardcoded hosts; user coords are numeric-validated and only fill query params (SMHI path uses toFixed)
verdictReason: Confirmed: assessed, not vulnerable. Hosts are constant literals: openMeteo.ts:43 `https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?${q}`, openMeteo.ts:57 `https://ensemble-api.open-meteo.com/v1/ensemble?${q}`, openMeteo.ts:120 multi-forecast, smhi.ts:15 with `lon = point.lon.toFixed(6)` (smhi.ts:13), metNorway.ts:12 `...?lat=${point.lat}&lon=${point.lon}`. Only user input reaching URLs is coords (rejected unless Number.isFinite and within lat[-90,90]/lon[-180,180], handler.ts:50-53) and a regex-constrained date (handler.ts:26,42). The SMHI path interpolation is safe because values pass through Number().toFixed(6) producing only digits/dot/optional-minus. No host is user-controlled.
evidence: openMeteo.ts:43,57,120 constant hosts; smhi.ts:13-15 `point.lon.toFixed(6)` then path-interpolated; metNorway.ts:12 coords in query; handler.ts:50-53 finite + lat/lon bound checks; handler.ts:26,42 ISO date regex gate.

title: @vercel/node pulls in 6 high-severity transitive vulnerabilities (undici, path-to-regexp, others)
verdictReason: The dependency chain is real and confirmed: package.json declares "@vercel/node": "^5.8.12" (actual line 26, NOT line 19 as cited) in root devDependencies, resolves to 5.8.12, and npm audit attributes all 9 advisories (undici, path-to-regexp 6.1.0, ajv, minimatch, smol-toml, @vercel/build-utils, @vercel/python-analysis, @vercel/static-config) to the @vercel/node subtree, with the offered 'fix' being a breaking downgrade to @vercel/node@4.0.0. However the severity and exploitability are overstated. (1) @vercel/node is a devDependency, not a runtime/production dependency. (2) api/weather.ts uses ONLY `import type { VercelRequest, VercelResponse } from '@vercel/node'` (types erased at build, zero runtime code). (3) The deployed function's outbound fetches go through global fetch via packages/core (gatherWindSamples -> Open-Meteo/SMHI/MET), NOT through @vercel/node's bundled undici 5.28.4. So the candidate's central exploitability claim ('undici request-smuggling/decompression issues are reachable from a deployed function making outbound fetches') is not substantiated. The risk is essentially build-time/dev-server only. Downgrading to a 4.x release as the audit suggests is debatable. Adjusted from high to medium.
evidence: package.json:26 "@vercel/node": "^5.8.12"; npm audit: "9 vulnerabilities (3 moderate, 6 high)" all chaining through node_modules/@vercel/node; api/weather.ts:1 `import type { VercelRequest, VercelResponse } from '@vercel/node';` (type-only); api/handler.ts uses packages/core global-fetch path, not @vercel/node undici; resolved undici 5.28.4, path-to-regexp 6.1.0.
recommendation: Treat as a dev/build-time advisory, not a production-runtime exposure (the type-only import means @vercel/node's undici/path-to-regexp never enter the serverless fetch path). Track upstream @vercel/node for a 5.x release that bumps undici/path-to-regexp/ajv rather than accepting npm's breaking @vercel/node@4.0.0 downgrade. Re-run `npm audit` after any bump. Note: the cited line number (19) is wrong; it is line 26.

title: riderNpAtSpeed slow-root: bisection returns implausibly slow speeds on steep descents (not the cited -3% multi-root mechanism)
verdictReason: The underlying bug is REAL and route-relevant, but the candidate's mechanism and example are wrong. I empirically reproduced riderNpAtSpeed(v) on a -3% descent as non-monotone (v=9->125.3W, v=12->70.2W) and solveSpeedForRiderNp(163,-0.08)=2.253 m/s (8.1 km/h) exactly as claimed. HOWEVER: (1) On the -3% grade the candidate emphasizes, the multi-root case actually has the bisection select the HIGHEST root (npTarget=110 -> v=14.34 m/s=51.6 km/h), not the slow root; and at the planner level the spin-out cap (vMax=50 km/h) binds and fully masks -3% descents. (2) The genuine failure is at STEEP descents (-6% to -18%): there riderNp(v) has a SINGLE low-speed root (e.g. -8%/npTarget=163 crosses 163 only at v~2.3, rising monotonically to a peak of 656W at v=13.5 and never returning below 163), so the solver returns the only root, a 3-10 km/h crawl, and the spin-out cap does NOT mask it because that speed is below vMax. End-to-end runInnerSolve on a -8% segment yields v=3.0-10 km/h (e.g. np=100 -> 4.9 km/h, t=1456s for 2 km). The real data/vatternrundan-315km.gpx route has 20 microsegments at <=-8% and 49 at <=-6% (down to -18%), so it is route-relevant.
evidence: chaingang.ts:302 comment 'riderNpAtSpeed is monotone increasing in v under normal conditions'; bisection chaingang.ts:319-323. Empirical: riderNpAtSpeed(12,-0.03)=70.2W < riderNpAtSpeed(9,-0.03)=125.3W (non-monotone); solveSpeedForRiderNp(163,-0.08)=2.253 m/s; runInnerSolve -8% seg at np=100 -> 4.9 km/h. Real route: 20 segs <=-8%.
recommendation: Fix the slow-root selection on steep descents, not the -3% multi-root case (the latter is masked by the spin-out cap and already picks the fast root). On a descent where the rider would coast/brake rather than pedal hard, the model should select the high-speed (coasting) regime or clamp to a coasting/braking speed rather than returning the low pedaling root that implies a 3-10 km/h descent. Update the misleading monotonicity comment at chaingang.ts:302. Severity remains high because steep descents on the real route produce physically absurd, time-inflating segment speeds.

title: Merged segment note can become inconsistent with its recomputed avg_grade
verdictReason: CONFIRMED and reproduced. mergeDisplaySegs recomputes avg_grade from summed heights/distance (line 183) but picks note from the dominant-distance half (line 193 `a.distance_m >= b.distance_m ? aNote : bNote`) without re-deriving against climb_threshold. The min_segment and max_segments passes have no note guard (only the grade-merge pass at line 468 enforces `a.note !== b.note`). My repro: a 4km climb (5%) merged with a 4km flat (0%) under maxSegments=2 produced a row note='SISTA UPPFÖR' (a climb label) with avg_grade=0.025, below climb_threshold=0.03 — note inconsistent with grade. Severity medium is appropriate (visibly wrong label on a pacing row, not a numeric pacing error).

recommendation: Re-derive note from the merged avg_grade and merged headwind in mergeDisplaySegs (reuse aggregateGroup's threshold logic, lines ~139-154), or refuse to merge rows with differing notes in the min_segment / max_segments passes the way the grade-merge pass already does at line 468.

title: avg_speed_kmh accumulates rounding drift across chained merges
verdictReason: CONFIRMED mechanism, impact correctly characterised as low. aggregateGroup rounds avg_speed_kmh to 0.1 km/h (line 163). mergeDisplaySegs reconstructs per-side time from this already-rounded speed (lines 216-217 `a.distance_m / (a.avg_speed_kmh / 3.6)`) and re-rounds (line 220), so chained merges compound the 0.05 km/h quantisation. micro_indices is carried on the row (line 239) but the true plan.segments[*].time_s is not used for merge math — accurate. I simulated 10 chained left-to-right merges with varied true speeds: true avg 29.6224 km/h vs merged 29.6000 km/h, error 0.0224 km/h — below display resolution (0.1 km/h). Real and confirmed, but practically negligible; severity low, confidence medium both fair.

title: avg_w weighted by full distance including neutral km, but excludes neutral power
verdictReason: CONFIRMED. aggregateGroup computes avg_w over only non-neutral segments (line 114 filter `!s.micro.neutral`, line 119 mean over effortSegs) but stores distance_m as the full group distance including neutral km (line 104). mergeDisplaySegs then re-weights avg_w by full distance_m (line 199). I verified neutral applies only to the route's first ~1km (gpx.ts line 141 `neutral = cumDist < cfg.neutral_distance_km * 1000`, default 1000m), so only the opening display segment mixes the neutral block with effort. The distance weight (incl. ~1 neutral km) does not match the power-sample population (effort segs only), slightly biasing the opening segment's avg_w. Impact is confined to one row at route start, as the candidate notes. Severity low, confidence medium both appropriate.
evidence: Line 104 `distance_m = segs.reduce((s, p) => s + p.micro.distance_m, 0)` (full, incl. neutral); lines 114/119 mean avg_w over effortSegs only; line 199 weights avg_w by full distance_m. gpx.ts line 141 confirms neutral is the first ~1km only.
recommendation: Weight avg_w by the effort (non-neutral) distance, or store an effort-distance field alongside distance_m so mergeDisplaySegs can weight consistently. Minor; affects only the opening ~1km segment.

title: Colliding control/stop snaps overwrite each other in controlAtCum/stopAtCum maps
verdictReason: CONFIRMED as a latent edge case. controlAtCum (lines 369-374) and stopAtCum (lines 377-381) are Maps keyed by snapped cum_distance_m; if two controls (or two stops) snap to the same micro boundary, Map.set keeps only the last, dropping the earlier town/stop from that boundary. The boundarySet (a Set, line 286) collapses the duplicate to one boundary/one group, and group conservation via groupStart (lines 342-357) is unaffected — accurately described. For the locked VATTERN_CONTROLS (~22-40km apart at ~315km) with fine micro resolution this cannot realistically collide; only near-identical configured stops would silently merge. Severity low, confidence medium both fair as a robustness note rather than a live bug.
evidence: Lines 373 `controlAtCum.set(snapped, cp)` and 380 `stopAtCum.set(snapped, stop.minutes)` — last-writer-wins on duplicate snapped keys. boundarySet (Set) and groupStart dedup grouping but not the town/stop identity per boundary.
recommendation: Detect snap collisions and warn or nudge to distinct boundaries. Low priority for the locked controls; matters only for misconfigured near-identical stop km values.

title: buildSplitTable uses km-based stopsBefore but name-based leg stop, which can desync
verdictReason: CONFIRMED as a latent robustness issue requiring misconfigured input. In buildSplitTable the cumulative stop time uses the stop's km field (line 54 `for (const s of cfg.stops) if (s.km < km) stopsBefore += s.minutes * 60`) while each leg's own stop is looked up by control NAME (lines 64-65 `stopByName.get(from.name)` / `get(to.name)`). The two paths reference the same stop set via different identities; if Stop.km disagrees with the control km, or Stop.control does not match a control name, arrive_s/depart_s can stop chaining. I verified that in solo mode controls are sourced directly from stops (cli.ts line 230 `controls.push({ name: stop.control, km: stop.km })`), so they cannot desync there; for the locked-VATTERN group path it relies on the operator configuring stops whose control/km match VATTERN_CONTROLS, and there is no validation enforcing this (config.ts validates only the three mandatory fields). Real but only triggerable by misconfiguration; severity low, confidence medium both appropriate.
evidence: splits.ts line 54 km-based `s.km < km` for stopsBefore vs lines 64-65 name-based `stopByName.get(from.name)`/`get(to.name)`. No stop-vs-control consistency validation in config.ts. Solo path (cli.ts line 230) derives controls from stops so is immune.
recommendation: Key both the cumulative and per-leg stop lookups off the same identity (match Stop.control to the controls array by name everywhere), or validate at config load that each Stop.control names a real control and Stop.km matches that control's km, so a misconfigured Stop.km cannot desync the cumulative time from the per-leg stop.

title: Timezone misalignment: local wall-clock start time matched against UTC weather hours
verdictReason: Independently confirmed end-to-end. types.ts:18 documents start_time as "local race-day time"; docs/research/2026-05-30-reference-pass-wind.md:12 confirms local = CEST = UTC+2 in summer. planner.ts:463 sets startClockS = clockToSeconds(cfg.start_time) (raw local clock, no UTC conversion) and passes it straight to makeWeatherFn. In ensemble.ts:237 queryHour = floor(((startClockS + timeS) % 86400)/3600) is therefore a LOCAL hour-of-day. Cells are fetched in UTC: openMeteo.ts:41,55 use timezone:'UTC'; smhi.ts:55/metNorway.ts:73 carry UTC ISO timestamps; hourOfDay (ensemble.ts:82-84) slices chars 11-13 = raw UTC hour. ensemble.ts:251-252 compares cellHour(UTC) to queryHour(local) with no offset compensation anywhere in the path. Systematic ~2h offset in summer. The cited line numbers in the candidate (229,243-246) are slightly off (the actual queryHour assignment is line 237 and the comparison is 251-254), but the code and claim are correct.
evidence: ensemble.ts:237 `const queryHour = Math.floor(((startClockS + timeS) % 86400) / 3600);` vs ensemble.ts:251-252 `const cellHour = hourOfDay(cell.time_iso); const hourDiff = Math.abs(cellHour - queryHour);` with openMeteo.ts:41 `timezone: 'UTC'` and types.ts:18 `start_time: string; // "04:22" local race-day time`.
recommendation: Convert the local start clock to UTC before computing queryHour (subtract the race-location UTC offset, +2h for Sweden in summer / DST-aware), or fetch and bin all weather in the same local timezone as start_time (e.g. Open-Meteo timezone=Europe/Stockholm and parse SMHI/MET into local hours). Note severity is high in principle but practical impact is bounded: the wind grid is hourly and selection is nearest-hour, so a 2h shift samples weather ~2 hours off the true time of day, biasing the diurnal wind/temp ramp; impact is largest near a steep morning wind ramp and around midnight wrap.

title: Open-Meteo parser emits no validation: null/NaN values and length-mismatched arrays poison ensemble means
verdictReason: The structural claim is confirmed: parseOpenMeteo (openMeteo.ts:86-98) iterates over times.length and blindly indexes parallel speeds/dirs/temps/pressures arrays with NO null/finite/length guards, in clear contrast to parseSmhi (smhi.ts:47-48 `if (ws===undefined||wd===undefined) continue;`) and parseMetNorway (metNorway.ts:65-66 same pattern). buildEnsemble accumulates without guards: ensemble.ts:147-153 sumU/sumV += derived from windspeed/dir, sumTemp += s.temp_c, sumPressure += s.pressure_pa, so a null/undefined sample yields NaN that propagates to windspeed_mean_ms/temp_c/pressure_pa for the whole cell (ensemble.ts:161,176-177). Open-Meteo genuinely can return null for unavailable hours, so this is reachable. Adjusting severity to MEDIUM: (a) the impact is confined to cells at the same rounded lat/lon/hour as the bad sample, not 'the whole race'; (b) when sources fetch the same race_date, hourly arrays from the forecast endpoint are normally complete, so the null/length-mismatch path is an edge case rather than a routine occurrence; (c) it degrades a value rather than crashing or corrupting persisted state. Still a real robustness gap worth fixing.
evidence: openMeteo.ts:91-94 `windspeed_ms: speeds[i], winddir_from_deg: dirs[i], temp_c: temps[i], pressure_pa: pressures[i] * 100,` with no guards, vs smhi.ts:47 `if (ws === undefined || wd === undefined) { continue; }`.
recommendation: Skip indices where windspeed_10m or winddirection_10m is null/undefined/non-finite (mirror the SMHI/MET parsers), and guard temp/pressure with finite-checks plus sensible defaults before pushing. Optionally add a finite-check in buildEnsemble's accumulation loop as defense in depth.

title: Calm fallback temperature/pressure are reasonable but wind direction 0 is silently treated as a real northerly
verdictReason: Confirmed as an info/low observation. The fallback (ensemble.ts:227-232) returns windspeed_ms:0, and the physics decomposes W=0 into headwind=W*cos(delta)=0 and crosswind=W*sin(delta)=0 (physics.ts:82-83), so winddir_from_deg:0 is indeed harmless when windspeed is 0. temp_c:10/pressure_pa:101325 give a plausible density. The genuine point stands: buildEnsemble computes reduced = allSources.size < 3 (ensemble.ts:183) but makeWeatherFn destructures only { cells } (ensemble.ts:223) and never reads field.reduced, so an all-empty fetch produces silent synthetic-calm planning with no distinct 'no data' signal. This is a UX/observability gap, not a correctness bug. Low severity is appropriate; really info-level.
evidence: ensemble.ts:227-231 `return (_lat, _lon, _timeS) => ({ windspeed_ms: 0, winddir_from_deg: 0, temp_c: 10, pressure_pa: 101_325, });` and ensemble.ts:223 `const { cells } = field;` (reduced never consulted).
recommendation: Surface a distinct 'no weather data' state to the planner/UI (e.g. propagate field.reduced or a cells.length===0 flag) rather than silently planning on synthetic calm, so users can tell a real calm forecast from a total source failure.

title: truncateToHour relies on fixed ISO offsets and silently mis-bins non-UTC or non-padded timestamps
verdictReason: The mechanism is correctly described: truncateToHour (ensemble.ts:73-75) slices chars 0-13 and hourOfDay (ensemble.ts:82-84) slices chars 11-13, both assuming a fixed-position zero-padded UTC hour; cellTimeIso = truncateToHour(rep.time_iso) + ':00:00Z' (ensemble.ts:143) unconditionally re-stamps as Z. If any source ever returned a +HH:MM-offset timestamp, the local hour would be grabbed and relabeled UTC. However the candidate itself acknowledges all current sources (SMHI/MET/Open-Meteo with timezone=UTC) return Z/UTC, so this is purely latent/fragility, not a current defect. Downgrading severity from medium to low: it is a defensive-coding/robustness concern with no present exploit. (Note: the separate live local-vs-UTC bug is finding #1, which is real today; this finding #4 is only the latent slicing fragility.)
evidence: ensemble.ts:75 `return timeIso.slice(0, 13);`, ensemble.ts:83 `const t = timeIso.slice(11, 13);`, ensemble.ts:143 `const cellTimeIso = truncateToHour(rep.time_iso) + ':00:00Z';`.
recommendation: Parse timestamps to a real epoch (Date.parse / Date.UTC) for binning and hour extraction so any numeric offset is honored, or assert/normalize that every incoming time_iso is UTC-Z before slicing. Latent today; harden before adding any non-UTC source.

title: Single-day fetch window: races crossing UTC midnight lose the post-midnight weather hours
verdictReason: Partly confirmed, partly weak. Confirmed: Open-Meteo URLs hard-code start_date=end_date=date (openMeteo.ts:41-42,54-55 and buildForecastUrlMulti 117-118), and gatherWindSamples passes a single date = cfg.race_date (fetchAll.ts:77-88; cli.ts:134). So the Open-Meteo forecast/ensemble series is clamped to one UTC calendar day. Cells are keyed/searched by hour-of-day only: nearest-time uses wrappedHourDiff (ensemble.ts:254) and hourOfDay ignores the date, so day N hour 02 and day N+1 hour 02 are interchangeable, and after-midnight segments reuse same-day-hour weather. That conflation is real. BUT two of the candidate's premises are shaky: (1) SMHI and MET are NOT date-clamped (their URLs take no date and return multi-day series, smhi.ts:12-16 / metNorway.ts:11-13), so for a midnight-crossing race those two sources DO provide next-day hours, and since cells are binned by hour-of-day the post-midnight hour still has data, just from fewer sources. (2) Vatternrundan starts are night/early-morning and the ride is ~9-12h, so for a typical config the elapsed clock crossing UTC midnight is plausible but the 'lose the hours entirely' framing overstates it given SMHI/MET coverage and hour-of-day binning. Net: a genuine day/hour-conflation and reduced-source-after-midnight issue, but lower impact than 'lose the post-midnight hours'. Severity medium->low.
evidence: openMeteo.ts:41-42 `start_date: date, end_date: date,` (also 54-55, 117-118); fetchAll.ts:77 `gatherWindSamples(points: GeoPoint[], date: string)`; ensemble.ts:254 `const wrappedHourDiff = Math.min(hourDiff, 24 - hourDiff);` (hour-of-day only, date ignored).
recommendation: Fetch Open-Meteo with start_date..end_date spanning the full race window (date and date+1 when the plan crosses midnight) and key cells by full date+hour rather than hour-of-day in the nearest-time search, so day N and day N+1 same-hour cells are distinguished and all sources cover the after-midnight segments.

title: GPX parser does no structural validation; malformed/empty GPX throws opaque TypeError or yields NaN points
verdictReason: Re-read gpx.ts:18-47. Line 20 `const gpx = doc['gpx'] as Record<string, unknown>` and line 23 `let trk = gpx['trk']` are unguarded: when the input lacks a <gpx> root, `gpx` is undefined and `gpx['trk']` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trk')`. The same applies to trkseg/trkpt down the chain. The map at lines 43-47 calls `Number(pt['@_lat'])` etc. with no NaN filter, so a trkpt missing @_lat or an absent <ele> yields NaN (Number(undefined)=NaN). ingestGpxString (line 170) feeds these straight into dedupePoints/haversine/smoothElevation/buildMicroSegments with no validation, and pipeline.ts:170 / cli.ts:115 are the untrusted file boundaries (web file.text(), CLI disk). No guard exists anywhere upstream. Holds as stated.
evidence: gpx.ts:20 `const gpx = doc['gpx'] as Record<string, unknown>;`; gpx.ts:23 `let trk = gpx['trk'];`; gpx.ts:43-46 `return points.map((pt) => ({ lat: Number(pt['@_lat']), lon: Number(pt['@_lon']), ele: Number(pt['ele']) }));`
recommendation: Guard each access (doc.gpx / trk / trkseg / trkpt) and throw a clear 'not a valid GPX file' error; after mapping, reject/drop points where lat/lon/ele is non-finite so NaN does not propagate silently through haversine and the physics solve.

title: GPX trk/trkseg multi-segment routes silently truncated to the first segment
verdictReason: Re-read gpx.ts:23-34. Lines 24-26 `if (Array.isArray(trk)) { trk = trk[0]; }` and 31-33 `if (Array.isArray(trkseg)) { trkseg = trkseg[0]; }` discard every segment after the first with no warning or flattening. A multi-<trk> or multi-<trkseg> GPX (routine from Strava/Garmin pauses, lap splits, or multi-track exports) keeps only segment [0], so a real route can be truncated to a fraction of its length and the plan silently solves the wrong distance. Claim holds. Severity medium is appropriate: wrong but plausible output, not a crash.
evidence: gpx.ts:24-26 `if (Array.isArray(trk)) { trk = trk[0]; }`; gpx.ts:31-33 `if (Array.isArray(trkseg)) { trkseg = trkseg[0]; }`
recommendation: Flatten all trk/trkseg trkpt arrays into one ordered point list, or at minimum warn when more than one segment is present and discarded.

title: time string parsers (hmToSeconds/clockToSeconds) accept any input and silently produce NaN
verdictReason: Re-read time.ts:10-22. hmToSeconds/clockToSeconds do `hm.split(':').map(Number)` with no validation; ''/'abc'/'11' (no colon -> m undefined -> NaN)/'11:' all yield NaN. Confirmed downstream in planner.ts:336 `const target = hmToSeconds(cfg.target_total_hm)`: with target=NaN, the unreachable check at line 344 `fastest.total_time_s > target` is false (any comparison with NaN is false), so it proceeds into the bisect loop where line 364 `Math.abs(plan.total_time_s - target) <= 20` is false and line 367 `plan.total_time_s > target` is false, so hi=mid for all 45 iterations and a meaningless `best` plan is returned with NO error. clockToSeconds(NaN) at planner.ts:335/463 corrupts every ETA via startClockS. target_total_hm/start_time are plain type=text inputs (UploadForm.tsx:316-324, 330-338) and raw config.json fields. Holds fully.
evidence: time.ts:10-12 `export function hmToSeconds(hm: string): number { const [h, m] = hm.split(':').map(Number); return h * 3600 + m * 60; }`; planner.ts:336 `const target = hmToSeconds(cfg.target_total_hm);`
recommendation: Validate format (e.g. ^\d+:\d{2}$) and finiteness in both parsers, throwing a clear error; or validate target_total_hm/start_time at the config/form boundary before they reach the solver.

title: Web form numeric fields (ftp, n_riders, m, stop km/minutes, styrkort_max_rows) use Number() with no NaN/zero/negative guard
verdictReason: The mechanism is confirmed but the cited line range is wrong. UploadForm.tsx:238-339 covers buildSubmit and the target/startTime text inputs, NOT the numeric onChange handlers. The actual `const v = Number(e.target.value)` handlers are at lines 371-374 (ftp), 385-389 (nRiders), 399-403 (m), 447-451 (styrkortMaxRows), and 543/551 (stop km/minutes). Number('') is NaN and number inputs can be cleared to empty; HTML min= (lines 369,384,398,446,542,550) is not enforced for typed/pasted/cleared values. These flow into PipelineForm (lines 250-264) -> applyDefaults (config.ts: pull_cap_hard=round(mult*ftp), pull_cap_soft=round(0.92*ftp)) and the solver range [60, cfg.ftp] (planner.ts:339), and NaN m breaks airDensity/pedalPower. Real and impactful; only the line numbers are off, so adjusted.
evidence: UploadForm.tsx:371-374 `onChange={(e) => { const v = Number(e.target.value); setFtp(v); persist({ ftp: v }); }}`; UploadForm.tsx:543 `onChange={(e) => updateStop(i, { km: Number(e.target.value) })}`
recommendation: Coerce each numeric field with a finite-fallback and clamp to sane minimums (ftp>=1, m>=1, n_riders>=1, etc.) before assembling PipelineForm, or block submit when any value is non-finite. Cited lines should be 371-403, 447-451, 543, 551.

title: applyDefaults validates only presence of the 3 mandatory string fields, never bounds of numeric config
verdictReason: Confirmed that applyDefaults (config.ts:58-101) validates only presence of gpx_path/race_date/start_time (lines 60-62) and applies no range/finiteness/type checks to any numeric field; raw values pass through via the spread at line 65. It is the single choke point for both CLI and web. The downstream consequences are real: neutral_speed_kmh=0 -> v=0 -> time_s=Infinity (planner.ts:133-134, verified); n_riders<=0 -> fFront returns 1/0=Infinity (chaingang.ts:17) and npMomentsFor divides by n=0 yielding NaN (chaingang.ts:239-244). The negative-max_grade sub-claim is slightly mischaracterised: with max_grade<0, `Math.max(-neg, Math.min(neg, x))` pins grade to the constant +|max_grade| rather than 'inverting the clamp', but it is still corruption. Severity high stands; details adjusted for the max_grade wording.
evidence: config.ts:60-62 presence-only checks; config.ts:81-86 `const ftp = raw.ftp ?? 272; ... const pull_cap_soft = raw.pull_cap_soft !== undefined ? raw.pull_cap_soft : Math.round(0.92 * ftp);`; planner.ts:133-134 `const v = cfg.neutral_speed_kmh / 3.6; const time_s = micro.distance_m / v;`
recommendation: Add finiteness + lower-bound validation here (ftp>=1, m>=1, n_riders>=1, neutral_speed_kmh>0, max_grade>=0, etc.) so every caller is protected. Note: a negative max_grade pins grade to a positive constant rather than inverting.

title: loadConfig does no try/catch around JSON.parse or readFileSync; type cast hides bad shapes
verdictReason: Re-read loadConfig.ts:13-16: `const raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8')) as RawConfig; return applyDefaults(raw);` with no try/catch and no object-shape assertion. A malformed config.json throws a raw SyntaxError; a bare array/number/null parses, is cast to RawConfig, and reaches applyDefaults where `!raw.gpx_path` (config.ts:60) works on a primitive but a non-object like a number would make property access return undefined (passing) rather than a clear error, and `null` would throw on the `!raw.gpx_path` only if raw is null (TypeError). Confirmed that cli.ts:107 calls loadConfig inside runPlan, and main()'s catch at cli.ts:282-283 prints `err.message`, so the user sees a low-level JSON parser message rather than 'config.json is not valid JSON'. Holds.
evidence: loadConfig.ts:14 `const raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8')) as RawConfig;`; cli.ts:283 `console.error(err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));`
recommendation: Wrap the read+parse in try/catch with a descriptive 'config.json is not valid JSON' error, and assert the parsed value is a non-null object before calling applyDefaults.

title: Weather cache file read trusts JSON.parse output as EnsembleField with no shape validation
verdictReason: Mechanism confirmed but line numbers are off: the cited code is at cache.ts:81-82, not 85-87 (file ends at line 84). readCache does `const raw = fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf-8'); return JSON.parse(raw) as EnsembleField;` with no try/catch and no shape check. A corrupt/truncated cache file (.cache/weather-<date>.json) throws an uncaught SyntaxError; verified this aborts the whole run even in --offline mode, because cli.ts:129 calls readCache unconditionally at the top of runPlan and the only catch is main()'s (cli.ts:282), which exits(1). A structurally wrong-but-valid JSON (e.g. cells missing) is cast and silently used downstream (makeWeatherFn reads field.cells). Real; severity medium fair. Adjusted only for the line citation (81-82).
evidence: cache.ts:81-82 `const raw = fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf-8'); return JSON.parse(raw) as EnsembleField;`; cli.ts:129 `let field: EnsembleField | null = readCache(cfg.race_date, cfg.cache_ttl_h, !!opts.offline);`
recommendation: Wrap the parse in try/catch returning null (treat corrupt file as cache miss), and verify Array.isArray(parsed.cells) before trusting it. Correct cited lines to cache.ts:81-82.

title: localStorage form state parsed and cast to PersistedForm with no field validation
verdictReason: Mechanism confirmed but line numbers are wrong: line 64 is `const LS_KEY = ...`; the cited code is at UploadForm.tsx:96-104 (loadFromStorage). The try/catch there only guards JSON syntax errors; the cast `return JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<PersistedForm>` does no shape/type validation. The parsed object seeds React state via `saved.ftp ?? FORM_DEFAULTS.ftp` (line 132) etc., so a stored ftp:'fast' or a malformed stops array survives the ?? guard (only null/undefined trigger the fallback, not a wrong-typed value) and flows into the pipeline where Number coercions can yield NaN. localStorage is user/extension-writable and persists across deploys. Real; severity medium reasonable. Adjusted for the line citation (96-104).
evidence: UploadForm.tsx:98-100 `const raw = localStorage.getItem(LS_KEY); if (!raw) return {}; return JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<PersistedForm>;`; UploadForm.tsx:132 `const [ftp, setFtp] = useState(saved.ftp ?? FORM_DEFAULTS.ftp);`
recommendation: Validate each restored field's type/range after parse and fall back to defaults per-field rather than trusting the cast (the ?? guard only catches null/undefined, not wrong types). Correct cited lines to 96-104.

title: FIT decoder output and power values are not bounds-checked; corrupt/non-FIT bytes throw uncaught in web pipeline
verdictReason: readFitPowerBytes (fit.ts:14-20) does `Stream.fromByteArray` + `new Decoder(stream).read()` with no try/catch, and filters power only by `typeof p === 'number'` (line 19), so garbage bytes from a renamed non-FIT file (UploadForm onFitChange reads any selected file as bytes, lines 188-198) throw inside read(), and negative/absurd power values pass the typeof filter and reach normalizedPower -> np_target. However the claim that the web worker has 'no try/catch (pipeline.ts:132)' is INACCURATE: pipeline.ts:184 calls readFitPowerBytes inside the async runPipeline, and solve.worker.ts:23-31 attaches a rejection handler (`.then(onFulfilled, (err) => postMessage({ ok:false, error: message }))`) that catches the throw and surfaces err.message. So it is not uncaught at the worker boundary; the user gets a raw library message, not a crash. Core issue (opaque error + unbounded power) is real; severity medium stands. Adjusted because the 'uncaught in web pipeline / pipeline.ts:132' detail is wrong.
evidence: fit.ts:15-19 `const stream = Stream.fromByteArray(Array.from(bytes)); const decoder = new Decoder(stream); const { messages } = decoder.read(); ... .filter((p): p is number => typeof p === 'number');`; solve.worker.ts:27-30 rejection handler posts `{ ok: false, error: message }` (the throw is caught, not uncaught)
recommendation: Wrap decode in try/catch with a clear 'not a valid FIT file' message and sanity-clamp/drop power samples (<0 or >~2000 W). Note the worker already converts the throw into an error message; the gap is the message quality and unbounded power, not an uncaught crash.

title: API /weather validates date format but not calendar validity or range
verdictReason: Re-read handler.ts:26,42. ISO_DATE = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ is a pure syntactic regex: it accepts 2026-13-40, 0000-00-00, 9999-99-99. The date is forwarded verbatim as start_date/end_date into buildForecastUrlMulti/buildEnsembleUrl/SMHI/MET (openMeteo.ts:38-41, fetchAll.ts) for the upstream fetches. These either error upstream (caught per-source, yielding []) or waste calls; no crash, hence low severity is correct. The note that lat/lon bounds (handler.ts:53) and MAX_POINTS (handler.ts:32,56) are correctly validated is accurate. Holds as a low-severity hardening item.
evidence: handler.ts:26 `const ISO_DATE = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/;`; handler.ts:42 `if (!date || !ISO_DATE.test(date) || !pts) return null;`
recommendation: Reject dates that do not round-trip through Date (e.g. new Date(date).toISOString().slice(0,10) === date) and optionally bound to a reasonable forecast window.

title: Open-Meteo/SMHI/MET parsers index parallel arrays without length checks; missing fields become NaN samples
verdictReason: Re-read openMeteo.ts:79-97. parseOpenMeteo loops `for (let i = 0; i < times.length; i++)` (line 86) and reads speeds[i]/dirs[i]/temps[i]/pressures[i] with no equal-length check and no numeric check. If the upstream returns time but a shorter/absent windspeed_10m, speeds[i] is undefined -> windspeed_ms NaN, and pressures[i]*100 (line 94) is NaN when surface_pressure is short/absent. These NaN WindSamples feed buildEnsemble (ensemble.ts:145-179, which sums with no finiteness guard -> NaN cell) and then makeWeatherFn -> the solver. The response is third-party/untrusted. Note the smhi/metNorway 'skip if ws/wd undefined' pattern (smhi.ts:47, metNorway.ts:65) guards undefined but NOT NaN, so it confirms the inconsistency the finding points at. Holds.
evidence: openMeteo.ts:86-94 `for (let i = 0; i < times.length; i++) { samples.push({ ... windspeed_ms: speeds[i], winddir_from_deg: dirs[i], ... pressure_pa: pressures[i] * 100, ... }); }`
recommendation: Skip entries where any required numeric field (speeds[i], dirs[i], temps[i], pressures[i]) is non-finite, and ideally guard NaN in smhi/metNorway too.

title: fetchOpenMeteo (per-point path) parses res.json() without checking res.ok
verdictReason: Confirmed at openMeteo.ts:176-191: the legacy per-point fetchOpenMeteo calls `await res.json()` (lines 178, 187) without an `if (!res.ok)` guard, unlike fetchOpenMeteoForecastBatched (line 152) and the fetchAll.ts wrappers (lines 46,56,66) which all check res.ok. A JSON error body returns [] (benign); a non-JSON error body makes res.json() throw, caught by the surrounding try/catch and silently dropping the source. HOWEVER, I grepped all production code: fetchOpenMeteo is referenced ONLY by tests (openMeteo.test.ts); the live weather path (gatherWindSamples in fetchAll.ts) uses fetchOpenMeteoForecastBatched + fetchOpenMeteoEnsemblePoint, both of which DO check res.ok. So this function is effectively dead in production. The candidate's own closing question ('Confirm whether this function is still reachable or dead code') is answered: it is dead. Real but near-zero impact; downgrading effective concern, severity low stays but it is dead-code cleanup, not a live bug.
evidence: openMeteo.ts:177-179 `const res = await fetch(buildForecastUrl(point, date)); const json = await res.json(); all.push(...parseOpenMeteo(json, point, 'open-meteo-forecast'));`; grep shows fetchOpenMeteo used only in tests/openMeteo.test.ts, not in fetchAll.ts or any handler
recommendation: Either delete fetchOpenMeteo as dead code (superseded by fetchAll.ts) or add `if (!res.ok) continue;` for consistency. Treat as low-priority cleanup, not a live-path fix.

title: makeWeatherFn / buildEnsemble assume finite numeric cells; one NaN sample poisons the whole field
verdictReason: Re-read ensemble.ts:145-179. The per-group loop sums s.windspeed_ms (via u/v at lines 147-148), s.temp_c (line 152), s.pressure_pa (line 153) and pushes s.windspeed_ms (line 151) with zero finiteness validation. A single NaN sample in a group makes sumU/sumV/sumTemp/sumPressure NaN, so that cell's windspeed_mean_ms/temp_c/pressure_pa (lines 161,176,177) are NaN. makeWeatherFn's combined score `distM/SPACE_REF_M + wrappedHourDiff/TIME_REF_H` (line 256) is unaffected by the NaN cell's wind values (score uses only lat/lon/time), but if that NaN cell wins the score it returns NaN wind into runInnerSolve. Chained with the parser finding, this is the propagation path. Holds; severity medium fair.
evidence: ensemble.ts:146-153 `const rad = toRad(s.winddir_from_deg); const u = -s.windspeed_ms * Math.sin(rad); ... sumTemp += s.temp_c; sumPressure += s.pressure_pa;`
recommendation: Filter non-finite WindSample numerics at ensemble entry (or validate WindCond before use in runInnerSolve) so one bad sample cannot poison a cell.

title: solveSpeedForPower returns midpoint silently when target power is unreachable in [0.5,25] m/s
verdictReason: Re-read physics.ts:45-62. The bisection clamps v to [0.5,25]; the loop (lines 54-60) only early-returns when |pm-target|<0.01, otherwise after 100 iterations it returns `(lo+hi)/2` (line 61) regardless of whether it converged. For a target the range cannot reach (huge headwind, near-zero cap) it converges to a boundary and returns it with no signal; any NaN target makes `Math.abs(pm-target)<0.01` false and `pm<target` false, so hi=mid each iteration and a boundary value is returned silently. The same pattern exists in solveSpeedForRiderNp (chaingang.ts:304-327). Confirmed; low severity is appropriate (degenerate-input quality issue, not a common crash).
evidence: physics.ts:54-61 `for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) { const mid = (lo + hi) / 2; const pm = pedalPower(...); if (Math.abs(pm - target) < 0.01) return mid; if (pm < target) lo = mid; else hi = mid; } return (lo + hi) / 2;`
recommendation: Detect non-convergence (final |pm-target| beyond tolerance) and surface it; short-circuit on non-finite target/grade/headwind inputs. Same applies to solveSpeedForRiderNp.

title: runInnerSolve divides distance by speed with no guard against zero/NaN neutral_speed or solved speed
verdictReason: Re-read planner.ts:133-134 (within the cited 116-135 range): `const v = cfg.neutral_speed_kmh / 3.6; const time_s = micro.distance_m / v;`. neutral_speed_kmh comes from config/defaults (DEFAULTS=20) with no validation (confirmed in config.ts). A user/config value of 0 makes v=0 and time_s=Infinity, which poisons elapsed/eta_s for every subsequent segment and total_time_s, breaking the outer bisection comparison. The effort-segment divisions at line 214 and 227 (`micro.distance_m / v`) likewise yield Infinity if a clamped/failed solve returns v=0 (the [0.5,25] floor makes v=0 unlikely from the solver, but vUncapped or a NaN-poisoned v from upstream still propagates). Core claim about neutral_speed=0 -> Infinity holds solidly; severity medium fair.
evidence: planner.ts:133-134 `const v = cfg.neutral_speed_kmh / 3.6; const time_s = micro.distance_m / v;`

title: parseOpenMeteo produces NaN/undefined WindSamples from partial/missing arrays; it is the only parser that does not skip incomplete rows
verdictReason: Re-read openMeteo.ts:79-98. The loop iterates over times.length and unconditionally reads speeds[i], dirs[i], temps[i], pressures[i]. If the API omits a field, that array defaults to [] (e.g. const pressures: number[] = h.surface_pressure ?? []), so pressures[i] is undefined for every i and pressure_pa: pressures[i] * 100 = NaN; windspeed_ms: speeds[i] is undefined. No continue/finite check. Cross-checked smhi.ts:47-49 and metNorway.ts:65-67: BOTH explicitly continue when ws/wd are undefined, confirming parseOpenMeteo is the lone parser that does not skip incomplete rows. This is the documented NaN entry point and feeds buildEnsemble unchecked.

[]; ... windspeed_ms: speeds[i], winddir_from_deg: dirs[i], ... pressure_pa: pressures[i] * 100. smhi.ts:47 if (ws === undefined || wd === undefined) { continue; }; metNorway.ts:65 same. parseOpenMeteo has no equivalent guard.
recommendation: Skip entries where windspeed/winddir are not finite (mirror parseSmhi/parseMetNorway continue), and default temp/pressure to sane constants when absent.

title: buildEnsemble has no NaN sanitation: one bad sample poisons cell mean wind, p10/p90, temp and pressure
verdictReason: Re-read ensemble.ts:145-179. The per-group accumulation (const u = -s.windspeed_ms * Math.sin(rad); sumU += u; ... speeds.push(s.windspeed_ms); sumTemp += s.temp_c; sumPressure += s.pressure_pa;) has zero finite checks (grep for isFinite/isNaN in ensemble.ts = 0). A single undefined windspeed_ms makes u = NaN, so sumU/sumV become NaN, meanU/meanV NaN, and windspeed_mean_ms = Math.hypot(NaN,NaN) = NaN and winddir_from_deg = NaN for the WHOLE cell (all samples grouped into that lat/lon/hour bin are polluted, not just the bad one). speeds.push(NaN) then speeds.sort corrupts the comparator ordering, so p10/p90 are unreliable. NaN pressure (from openMeteo finding) flows here as sumPressure. Holds exactly as claimed.
evidence: ensemble.ts:146-153 (no guard), ensemble.ts:161 const windspeed_mean_ms = Math.hypot(meanU, meanV);, ensemble.ts:164 speeds.sort((a, b) => a - b); with possible NaN entries.
recommendation: Filter group samples to finite windspeed/dir/temp/pressure before aggregation, or guard each accumulation, so one malformed upstream sample cannot NaN an entire cell that makeWeatherFn may then select.

title: Physics and planner have zero NaN guards; a NaN weather value silently yields NaN power/time with no error
verdictReason: Re-read physics.ts and planner.ts; grep -c for isFinite|isNaN|Number.isNaN returned 0 for both files (and for hourly.ts, ensemble.ts, gpx.ts). pedalPower (physics.ts:23-38) computes const u = v + headwind; const vApp = Math.hypot(u, crosswind); const fAero = 0.5*p.rho*p.cda*vApp*u; and returns NaN unchecked if headwind/crosswind is NaN. solveSpeedForPower (physics.ts:45-62) bisects on if (pm < target) lo = mid; else hi = mid; where NaN < target is false, so a NaN power steers the solver into the else branch every iteration and it returns (lo+hi)/2 with no error surfaced. The cited line 20-33 is slightly off (the NaN-prone arithmetic is lines 33-35, and the silently-wrong solver is 45-62); adjusting the line span to 23-62. Severity high stands: a NaN cell selected by makeWeatherFn flows straight into a NaN/garbage plan rendered as blank cells.
evidence: physics.ts:33-35 const u = v + headwind; const vApp = Math.hypot(u, crosswind); const fAero = 0.5 * p.rho * p.cda * vApp * u;; physics.ts:56-59 bisection compares Math.abs(pm - target) < 0.01 and pm < target (both false for NaN).
recommendation: Add a finite-value guard at the weather/physics boundary (treat non-finite WindCond as calm) so a malformed upstream value degrades to calm instead of producing a NaN plan the UI renders blank.

title: parseGpxString throws cryptic 'Cannot read properties of undefined' on non-GPX / malformed XML; no validation
verdictReason: Re-read gpx.ts:18-41. const gpx = doc['gpx'] as Record<string, unknown>; then let trk = gpx['trk'];. If the uploaded file is not GPX (no top-level <gpx>), doc['gpx'] is undefined and gpx['trk'] throws a raw TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading trk)'. No existence check on gpx/trk/trkseg/trkpt. The cast to Record<string, unknown> is compile-time only and does not prevent the runtime throw. In the web flow this throw is caught by App.doFetch's bare catch and (in fetched mode) mislabeled (see separate finding); in the worker/run path it surfaces as the raw message. Confirmed as a missing-validation issue producing a cryptic message.

recommendation: Validate the parsed structure and throw a clear message such as 'Not a valid GPX file (no <trk> found)' so the user-facing error is actionable.

title: GPX trackpoints with missing lat/lon/ele become NaN coordinates that flow silently into haversine and the solver

Confirmed; severity medium is fair since a fully-malformed GPX is operator/user error but degrades silently.

recommendation: Drop or reject points whose lat/lon are non-finite and default ele to 0, so a partially-malformed GPX fails loudly or skips bad points instead of emitting NaN distances.

title: App.doFetch wraps GPX ingest + sampling inside the weather-fetch try/catch, so a GPX parse error is mislabeled 'Hamtning misslyckades' (fetch failed)

[]` etc., line 86 loops `for (let i = 0; i < times.length; i++)` on times.length only, line 91 `windspeed_ms: speeds[i]`, line 94 `pressure_pa: pressures[i] * 100`. title: makeWeatherFn does an O(cells) haversine scan per query: tens of millions of haversine calls per run, dominant cost of the ~8s solve
verdictReason: Code confirmed exactly: the returned closure runs `for (const cell of cells) { const distM = haversine(...) }` (line 249-250) over all cells on every query, and haversine is a genuine 2-sin/2-cos/asin/sqrt call (util/geo.ts:24-27). I re-ran the repo's bench_tmp.mts: solveThreeScenarios with wind = 8787 ms (candidate said 7342; even worse), makeWeatherFn x10000 = 494 ms (~49us/call), ensemble cells = 704 (matches). However bench2/my bench3 measured 28164 weather calls per solveForTargetTime (1 stop), not 32858, giving ~19.8M haversine evals per solve and ~59M (not 69.4M) across 3 scenarios. The dominant-cost claim is solid, but the call/eval counts were overstated and the per-run number depends on stop count, so I downgrade critical->high. Cells ARE already binned via roundCoord (0.1deg, line 66-67) and truncateToHour, so the proposed Map-keyed O(1) index is feasible; care is only needed because the current code picks the globally nearest cell via a combined space+time score, so a fixed-radius fallback must preserve the cross-bin nearest-neighbour behaviour.
evidence: ensemble.ts:249-250 `for (const cell of cells) { const distM = haversine({ lat, lon }, { lat: cell.lat, lon: cell.lon }); ... }`; util/geo.ts:24-27 haversine uses Math.sin/cos/asin/sqrt. Reproduced: cells=704, solveThreeScenarios=8787ms, 28164 weather calls/solve -> ~19.8M haversine/solve.
recommendation: Precompute a Map keyed by `${roundCoord(lat)}|${roundCoord(lon)}|${hour}` once when makeWeatherFn is built (cells are already on that exact grid), then O(1) lookup with a bounded-radius fallback that reproduces the existing combined-score nearest-cell choice. This collapses the per-query O(704) haversine scan and should cut the dominant cost by ~1-2 orders of magnitude. Verified eval counts are tens of millions per run, not the cited 69M, but the win stands.

title: solveThreeScenarios runs three independent full bisections from the same [60,ftp] range with no warm-start
verdictReason: The cross-scenario redundancy is real and confirmed: solveScenario is called for expected/optimistic/pessimistic (planner.ts:471-473), each a full solveForTargetTime bisecting the SAME [60, ftp] range (planner.ts:356-357), plus 2 extra runInnerSolve marches for the time interval (lines 480-493). title: Segmentation merge passes are superlinear via while-changed full-restart scans with slice rebuilds
verdictReason: Confirmed exactly as described. Two `while (changed) { ... for (...) { ...; changed = true; break; } }` loops (segmentation.ts:414-445 minSegmentKm merge, 461-475 grade merge) restart the whole scan from index 0 after every single merge, and each merge rebuilds the array via spread+slice: `displaySegs = [...displaySegs.slice(0, lo), merged, ...displaySegs.slice(hi + 1)]` (line 441, also line 471 and the maxSegs loop at line 505). recommendation: Replace restart-on-merge with a single left-to-right in-place sweep (or a priority queue keyed by avg_w diff) for O(n log n). Low priority at current n, but it is the only structurally superlinear hot path; worth it only if many-micro-boundary routes appear.

title: Wind hour table direction input accepts 0-360 but rejects degrees with no inline validation, and arrow rotation can be visually misleading
verdictReason: Confirmed. The direction input has only native min={0} max={360} with no clamp/normalize on typed entry (browsers do not hard-clamp typed numbers), and compass() uses deg%360 (WindHourTable.tsx:18) so a typed 999 produces no inline feedback. The input itself does have aria-label (`riktning ${r.hour}`), matching the candidate. Low severity is appropriate.

title: Weather mode toggle uses div+buttons without aria-pressed / radio semantics
verdictReason: Confirmed. The seg-toggle is a div role="group" aria-label="Väderläge" (WeatherPanel.tsx:42) with three <button> children whose only selected-state cue is className={mode === m ? 'active' : ''} (line 47). title: Manual-wind 'Riktning°'/'Styrka m/s' labels wrap the input but have no programmatic separation; constant-apply has no confirmation
verdictReason: Confirmed. The 'Riktning°' and 'Styrka m/s' labels nest their inputs (implicit label, acceptable) at WeatherPanel.tsx:100-119. 'Applicera på alla timmar' (line 120-122) calls onApplyConstant -> App.applyConstant (App.tsx:110-115) which destructively replaces every baseRows entry and clears all overrides (setOverrides(new Map())) with no confirmation, undo, or status message; the only feedback is the table silently re-rendering. Matches the finding. Candidate's App.tsx line cite (86-91) is stale; actual is 110-115.
evidence: WeatherPanel.tsx:120-122 `<button type="button" onClick={() => props.onApplyConstant(constDir, constSpeed)}>Applicera på alla timmar</button>`. App.tsx:110-115 applyConstant sets `setBaseRows(rows); setOverrides(new Map());` with no status emit.

title: Disabled buttons rely on opacity only; no global :focus-visible styling for custom buttons
verdictReason: Confirmed. A grep of styles.css shows no :focus-visible (or :focus) rule anywhere; the custom .primary/.ghost/.run-button/.link/.download-btn rely solely on the UA default focus outline. Disabled state is only opacity:0.5 (button.primary:disabled styles.css:188-191; .run-button:disabled 325-328). For keyboard users tabbing across the card-on-white layout, focus visibility on these custom controls is whatever the browser default provides, which is weak against the low-contrast ghost borders. Finding holds; cited line ranges are close enough (286-293 in candidate maps to the spinner/keyframes block, the relevant rules are 316-328 for run-button).
evidence: No `:focus-visible` match in styles.css. button.primary:disabled styles.css:188-191 `opacity: 0.5`. .run-button:disabled 325-328 `opacity: 0.5`. button.ghost 193-203 has only a border + hover rule, no focus rule.
recommendation: Add an explicit :focus-visible outline (e.g. 2px solid var(--accent) with offset) for .primary, .ghost, .run-button, .link, and .download-btn so keyboard focus is clearly visible against the white cards.

title: Large data tables scroll horizontally on mobile with no scroll affordance or sticky header
verdictReason: Partly confirmed, partly mitigated. Confirmed: both big tables wrap in `<div className="table-scroll">` { overflow-x: auto } (SplitTable.tsx:20, TempokortTable.tsx:94, styles.css:234-236) with no sticky thead, no sticky first column, and no visible scroll-shadow hint. However the candidate overstates the mobile pain: styles.css:628-643 hides .col-secondary columns on <=640px, dropping the split table from 8 to 5 columns and the full tempokort to fewer columns, which materially reduces horizontal overflow. So the 'no scroll affordance' and 'no sticky label column' points stand, but the '8/10 columns on a phone' framing is inaccurate. Severity low is correct.
evidence: SplitTable.tsx:20 `<div className="table-scroll">`; styles.css:234-236 `.table-scroll { overflow-x: auto; }` (no sticky). styles.css:628-643 @media (max-width: 640px) hides th/td.col-secondary. SplitTable marks 3 of 8 columns col-secondary (lines 29-31); TempokortTable marks several col-secondary (134-148).
recommendation: On narrow viewports add a scroll-shadow/indicator and consider position: sticky on the first column (Sträcka / Sektion) so row identity stays visible. Note the existing col-secondary hiding already trims the column count on mobile.

title: Compact/full Tempokort toggle is low-discoverability and uses inline styles for the stop-row color cue
verdictReason: Partly confirmed, mostly refuted on the color-only claim. Confirmed: the view toggle is a single ghost button labeled 'Visa fullständigt'/'Visa styrkortsläge' (TempokortTable.tsx:84) rather than a visible 2-option segmented control, so both states are not simultaneously visible (mild discoverability concern, though an adjacent InfoTip at 87-91 now explains the two views). So the WCAG 1.4.1 color-only concern is already mitigated and the inline-style claim is false.

'Visa fullständigt' : 'Visa styrkortsläge'}</button>`; 87-91 adjacent InfoTip. 111/157 `className={seg.stop_minutes ? 'stop-row' : undefined}` (CSS class, not inline). 117/163 `{seg.stop_minutes ? '☕ ' : ''}` non-color marker. styles.css:583-586 .stop-row { background: #fff3cd; font-weight: 600 }.
recommendation: Optionally make the toggle a visible 2-option segmented control for discoverability. No fix needed for the stop-row encoding: it already pairs background color with a ☕ icon and a CSS class. Correct the candidate's inline-style and color-only claims.

title: Target time / start time use free-text inputs with no validation feedback for malformed h:mm input
verdictReason: Confirmed (line numbers shifted to 316-324 and 330-338). Both Måltid and Starttid are `<input type="text" ... placeholder="11:45"/` and `placeholder="04:22"/>` with no pattern, no inputmode, no aria-invalid, and no inline error messaging. A malformed value would only surface downstream as a solver error shown via the generic error card (App.tsx:236-241). Finding holds; note the current placeholders are '11:45'/'04:22' (candidate cited '2:30'/'06:00', which are the older defaults but the structural point is unchanged).
evidence: UploadForm.tsx:316-323 target input `<input type="text" value={targetTotalHm} ... placeholder="11:45" />` (no pattern/inputmode/validation). 330-337 start input `<input type="text" value={startTime} ... placeholder="04:22" />`.
recommendation: Add inputmode="numeric", a pattern (e.g. \d{1,2}:\d{2}) and inline validation with aria-invalid + a hint, so malformed time entry is caught at the field rather than as an opaque downstream compute error.
