title: No Node version pinning (.nvmrc / package.json engines absent); CI hardcodes Node 22 while local/Vercel are unconstrained
verdictReason: Re-verified: ci.yml:12 has `node-version: '22'`. `grep engines` across package.json (only root package.json exists with workspaces) returns nothing, and there is no .nvmrc / .node-version at repo root. Drift risk is real, but severity is overstated. devDeps target @types/node ^25 and typescript ^6 (package.json:25,35), but the only outputs are a static web bundle (build:web -> apps/web/dist) plus a dep-light Vercel serverless function. No published library / strict runtime ABI dependency, so practical blast radius is limited. Lowered medium -> low.
evidence: ci.yml:12 `node-version: '22'`; root package.json has no `engines` key (devDeps include `@types/node`: `^25.9.1`, `typescript`: `^6.0.3`); no .nvmrc/.node-version at repo root.
recommendation: Add `engines.node` (e.g. ">=22") to root package.json and a `.nvmrc`/`.node-version` pinning the major, then reference it from setup-node via `node-version-file`. Vercel default Node and contributor local Node can otherwise drift from CI's Node 22.

title: CI runs no lint step (ESLint is configured but never enforced in CI)
verdictReason: Candidate's core evidence is FALSE: it claims 'no ESLint config exists' and no `lint` script. Re-verified: eslint.config.js exists (flat config: typescript-eslint, react-hooks, react-refresh, prettier) and package.json:17 defines `"lint": "eslint ."`. The premise is wrong, BUT the underlying gap is real: ci.yml:15-17 runs only typecheck/test/build:web with NO `npm run lint` step. Lint is enforced solely via a bypassable lefthook pre-commit hook (lefthook.yml `lint` job, --fix, staged files only). So CI has no lint gate. Adjusted to the accurate framing; severity kept medium because wiring lint into CI is low effort but several rules are 'warn' not 'error', so the gate would be weak without rule tightening.
evidence: ci.yml:15-17 runs only `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build:web` (no lint step). eslint.config.js exists; package.json:17 `"lint": "eslint ."`. Lint enforcement only in lefthook.yml pre-commit (`npx eslint --fix {staged_files}`), local and bypassable.
recommendation: Add an `npm run lint` step to ci.yml as a required PR gate. Note several rules (`no-explicit-any`, `no-useless-assignment`, `react-refresh/only-export-components`) are 'warn' and won't fail the build; promote correctness-critical ones to 'error' for a real gate.

title: CI has no dependency vulnerability gate (no `npm audit` / Dependabot)
verdictReason: Re-verified: ci.yml runs `npm ci` (line 14) then typecheck/test/build only, no `npm audit`. `.github/` contains only `workflows/`; no dependabot.yml. So the gate genuinely does not exist. Supply-chain framing is partially overstated: api/weather.ts is a thin adapter and handler.ts:5-12 deliberately imports deep pure modules to keep npm deps out of the serverless bundle, so the prod serverless dep surface is intentionally minimal; the browser bundle is the larger surface. Real but lower impact; medium -> low.
evidence: ci.yml:14 `npm ci`; no `npm audit`/audit-level step; `.github/` has only `workflows/` (no dependabot.yml).
recommendation: Add `npm audit --audit-level=high` to CI and/or commit `.github/dependabot.yml` plus the dependency-review action on PRs. Primary unaudited surface is the browser bundle's transitive deps (the serverless handler is intentionally dep-light per handler.ts:5-12).

title: No test coverage measurement or coverage gate
verdictReason: Re-verified: vitest.config.ts defines `projects` (unit + web, lines 16-32) but no `test.coverage` block. No coverage/c8/istanbul references in package.json or vitest.config.ts. CI runs `npm test` = `vitest run` (package.json:11) with no `--coverage`. eslint.config.js:16 ignores `coverage/**`, hinting coverage was anticipated but never wired up. Claim holds; low severity appropriate.
evidence: vitest.config.ts:13-34 has `test.projects` but no `coverage` key; package.json:11 `"test": "vitest run"` (no coverage flag); no coverage/c8/istanbul references anywhere.
recommendation: Add `test.coverage` (provider 'v8') with thresholds for packages/core (the correctness-critical physics/planner math) and run `vitest run --coverage` in CI to fail on regressions.

title: Two competing lockfiles present (pnpm-lock.yaml + package-lock.json); pnpm-workspace.yaml in working tree (gitignored)
verdictReason: Candidate's specific evidence is FALSE in two ways. (1) It claims pnpm-workspace.yaml is placeholder garbage `allowBuilds:\n  esbuild: set this to true or false`. The actual file has REAL content (allowBuilds with esbuild/lefthook, minimumReleaseAgeExclude pinning @vercel/build-utils@13.27.1 and @vercel/node@5.8.12), not a malformed placeholder. (2) It claims the files are 'committed to the tree'; in fact .gitignore:3-5 ignores both pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml, and `git ls-files` confirms ONLY package-lock.json is tracked (pnpm files are untracked local artifacts). Vercel auto-detection concern is moot because vercel.json sets `installCommand: npm install`, overriding package-manager detection, and Vercel builds from the git checkout (which lacks the gitignored pnpm files). Residual issue is minor local hygiene only. Downgraded to info and corrected the false evidence. (The `lockfileVersion: '9.0'` detail was the only accurate part.)
evidence: pnpm-workspace.yaml:1-6 contains real pnpm config (allowBuilds, minimumReleaseAgeExclude), NOT the claimed placeholder text. .gitignore:3-5 ignores pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml ('this repo uses npm'). `git ls-files | grep lock` returns only `package-lock.json`. pnpm-lock.yaml header is `lockfileVersion: '9.0'`.
recommendation: Optional local hygiene: delete the untracked pnpm-lock.yaml / pnpm-workspace.yaml from the working tree to avoid confusing local pnpm runs. No repo-level or deploy-level impact: both are gitignored, only package-lock.json is tracked, and vercel.json pins the install command to npm.

title: Vercel uses non-deterministic install (`npm install`) instead of lockfile-pinned `npm ci`
verdictReason: Re-verified: vercel.json:5 `"installCommand": "npm install"` vs ci.yml:14 `npm ci`. Mismatch and reproducibility concern (npm install can mutate the lockfile / pick newer in-range versions) are accurate. Severity 'medium' is slightly high: the repo ships a static bundle plus a dep-light serverless function, and the tracked lockfile still constrains resolution. Defect is real, fix is trivial. medium -> low.
evidence: vercel.json:5 `"installCommand": "npm install"`; ci.yml:14 `npm ci`. package-lock.json tracked.
recommendation: Set vercel.json `installCommand` to `npm ci` so production builds resolve strictly from package-lock.json and match what CI tested.

title: Serverless function (api/) has no runtime/region/maxDuration/memory configuration
verdictReason: Re-verified: vercel.json (lines 1-6) declares only $schema/buildCommand/outputDirectory/installCommand, no `functions` block. handler.ts:28-32 documents the fan-out (1 + 3N upstream fetches per cache miss, MAX_POINTS=64 at handler.ts:32). With no declared maxDuration the function relies on Vercel project/plan defaults, and a slow upstream (Open-Meteo/SMHI/MET) can hit the default timeout. There IS an s-maxage=10800 cache header (handler.ts:25) mitigating repeat latency, but cold/cache-miss fan-out is unbounded by config. Claim holds; low severity appropriate.
evidence: vercel.json:1-6 has no `functions` block. handler.ts:28-32 describes 1+3N upstream fetches per cache miss; handler.ts:32 `const MAX_POINTS = 64;`; handler.ts:25 sets s-maxage=10800 cache header.
recommendation: Add a `functions` block pinning the Node runtime and a maxDuration, e.g. `"api/*.ts": {"runtime": "nodejs22.x", "maxDuration": 30}`, so timeout/runtime don't drift with Vercel defaults and slow upstreams fail predictably.

title: CI triggers on every push to every branch with no concurrency control or path filtering
verdictReason: Re-verified: ci.yml:2-4 is `on:`/`push:`/`pull_request:` with no `branches`/`paths` filter, and grep for concurrency/branches/paths returns NONE. Every push to any branch runs the full job, and a branch with an open PR runs it twice (push + pull_request) with no cancel-in-progress. Claim holds; low severity (cost/efficiency) appropriate.
evidence: ci.yml:2-4 `on:`/`push:`/`pull_request:` with no filters; no top-level `concurrency:` key (grep returned NONE).
recommendation: Add `concurrency: { group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` and scope `push` to main + tags (PRs already cover feature branches) to stop double-runs and stale-run waste.

title: GitHub Actions has no minimal permissions block (defaults to broad GITHUB_TOKEN scopes)
verdictReason: Re-verified: no top-level or job-level `permissions:` key anywhere in ci.yml (grep returned NONE). The job only checks out/installs/typechecks/tests/builds, needing read access only. Without an explicit block, GITHUB_TOKEN scopes default to the repo/org Actions setting (can be read-write). Valid hardening gap; low severity correct (defense-in-depth, no untrusted code runs with the token).
evidence: ci.yml has no `permissions:` key at workflow or job level (grep returned NONE). Steps are checkout/setup-node/npm ci/typecheck/test/build only.
recommendation: Add `permissions: { contents: read }` at the workflow top level to drop unneeded write scopes from GITHUB_TOKEN.

title: Actions are pinned only to mutable major tags (@v4), not commit SHAs
verdictReason: Re-verified: ci.yml:9 `uses: actions/checkout@v4` and ci.yml:10 `uses: actions/setup-node@v4`, both mutable major tags, not full commit SHAs. Both are first-party GitHub-owned actions (lower compromise likelihood than third-party), which is why low severity fits, but the hardening point is valid: a moved/compromised tag would run in CI with the repo token. Claim holds.
evidence: ci.yml:9 `uses: actions/checkout@v4`; ci.yml:10 `uses: actions/setup-node@v4`.
recommendation: Pin actions to full commit SHAs (e.g. `actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`) and let Dependabot bump them. Lower urgency since both are GitHub-owned first-party actions.

title: 'Files stay in your browser, nothing uploaded' claim is accurate for GPX/FIT
verdictReason: Substantively CONFIRMED but with a wrong citation that must be corrected. onGpxChange reads `await file.text()` (UploadForm.tsx:183) and onFitChange reads `await file.arrayBuffer()` (UploadForm.tsx:195) into local React state; there is no upload of gpxText/fitBytes. The only browser egress is weatherClient.ts fetch('/api/weather?...') carrying derived coordinates only. HOWEVER the candidate's cited line range 127-145 is wrong (those lines are state declarations and buildSubmit, not the file readers), and it quotes App.tsx:136 with ENGLISH text 'Uploaded GPX and FIT files are processed entirely in your browser and never uploaded'. That English string does not exist: App.tsx:136 is inside handleRun (a code comment about height correction), and the real privacy note is Swedish at App.tsx:195-199 ('Uppladdade GPX- och FIT-filer behandlas helt i din webbläsare och laddas aldrig upp ... Lugnt och manuellt läge skickar ingenting'). The underlying privacy guarantee holds; the line refs and the quoted English text are inaccurate.
evidence: UploadForm.tsx:183 `const text = await file.text();`; UploadForm.tsx:195 `const buffer = await file.arrayBuffer();`; only outbound fetch is weatherClient.ts:18 `await fetch(\`/api/weather?date=...&pts=...\`)`. Real privacy note: App.tsx:196 'Uppladdade GPX- och FIT-filer behandlas helt i din webbläsare och laddas aldrig upp.'
recommendation: Keep the verification: GPX text and FIT bytes never leave the browser. Correct the citation to UploadForm.tsx:180-198 for the readers and App.tsx:195-199 for the (Swedish) privacy note.

title: Coordinates sent to /api/weather are correctly rounded to 0.1deg before leaving the browser
verdictReason: CONFIRMED with a minor line correction. weatherClient.ts:4-6 roundPt does `lat: Math.round(p.lat * 10) / 10, lon: Math.round(p.lon * 10) / 10`; buildPtsParam (lines 8-13) maps every point through roundPt before joining into the pts query string, and fetchEnsemble uses buildPtsParam. So the browser->server payload is coarsened to ~0.1deg (~11 km) cells, as claimed. The defense-in-depth observation is also correct: sampleCellPoints (sample.ts:17-27) emits FULL-precision segment-start coords (points.push({ lat: m.lat, lon: m.lon }) with no rounding), so rounding exists only at the client request boundary. Cited range adjusted from 3-10 to 3-13 to cover buildPtsParam.
evidence: weatherClient.ts:5 `return { lat: Math.round(p.lat * 10) / 10, lon: Math.round(p.lon * 10) / 10 };`; weatherClient.ts:9-12 `.map(roundPt).map((p) => \`${p.lat},${p.lon}\`).join('|')`. sample.ts:24 `points.push({ lat: m.lat, lon: m.lon });` (unrounded).
recommendation: No functional change required. Optionally round at sampleCellPoints too for defense-in-depth, so any future caller that bypasses buildPtsParam cannot leak full-precision coordinates.

title: Rounded route coordinates are forwarded to three external third parties (SMHI, MET Norway, Open-Meteo) by the server
verdictReason: CONFIRMED. gatherWindSamples (fetchAll.ts:77-88) fans out via Promise.all to fetchOpenMeteoForecastBatched + per-point fetchOpenMeteoEnsemblePoint + fetchSmhi + fetchMetNorway. fetchSmhi calls buildSmhiUrl -> opendata-download-metfcst.smhi.se (smhi.ts:15); fetchMetNorway calls buildMetNorwayUrl -> api.met.no (metNorway.ts:12) with header User-Agent `StickToThePlan/1.0 (https://github.com/timcv/StickToThePlan)` (metNorway.ts:31 + DEFAULT_MET_NORWAY_CONTACT); Open-Meteo hits api.open-meteo.com (openMeteo.ts:43,120) and ensemble-api.open-meteo.com (openMeteo.ts:57). handler.ts:69 passes parsed.points (already 0.1deg-rounded by the client) to gatherWindSamples. smhi.ts:13-14 toFixed(6) only formats already-coarse inputs, exposing no extra precision. Severity low is appropriate: coarse (~11 km) coords + date, no identifiers; this is exactly what the README and App.tsx already disclose. Note the request CAN bypass the client rounding (any direct caller of /api/weather), but handler.ts validates and caps points and the data carries no PII, so impact stays low.
evidence: fetchAll.ts:80-85 Promise.all of forecast+ensemble+smhi+met; smhi.ts:15 `https://opendata-download-metfcst.smhi.se/...`; metNorway.ts:12 `https://api.met.no/weatherapi/locationforecast/2.0/compact?lat=...`; metNorway.ts:31 `'User-Agent': \`StickToThePlan/1.0 (${contact})\``; openMeteo.ts:43/57 open-meteo hosts.
recommendation: No change required; all three upstreams are already disclosed in App.tsx:198 and README.md:111. Data shared is coarse and identifier-free.

title: Real high-precision Vätternrundan GPS track committed to public repo and bundled into web app
verdictReason: CONFIRMED. examples/vattern-315.gpx is a single-line GPX with 4820 <trkpt> elements (~443 KB) containing full-precision coordinates, e.g. first point `<trkpt lat="58.53586267111379" lon="15.038557715124384"><ele>106.6438980102539</ele>` (15-decimal lat/lon + elevation). It is named 'Vätternrundan 315 km' and the start (58.5359,15.0386) and end (58.5350,15.0338) cluster in central Motala, the official Vätternrundan start/finish area, which points to the sanctioned public event course rather than a private home start. defaultRoute.ts:8 imports it via `'../../../../examples/vattern-315.gpx?raw'` so it is inlined into the public web bundle and prefilled as the default route (UploadForm.tsx:123 seeds gpxText with defaultRouteGpx). The candidate's factual claims hold; severity low is fair since the route appears to be the public event course, not a personal export.
evidence: examples/vattern-315.gpx:1 first trkpt lat=58.53586267111379 lon=15.038557715124384 ele=106.6438980102539; 4820 trkpt elements; last trkpt lat=58.535041 lon=15.033785. defaultRoute.ts:8 `import defaultRouteGpx from '../../../../examples/vattern-315.gpx?raw';`
recommendation: Confirm in repo docs that this is the official/public Vätternrundan event course (start/finish in Motala) rather than an individual's recorded ride, so the committed full-precision track carries no personal home-location exposure. If derived from a personal recording, trim/sanitize start and end. Low risk given it matches the public event start area.

title: localStorage stores only rider parameters, not route/file data
verdictReason: CONFIRMED with a minor line correction (50-80 -> 64-112). LS_KEY = 'stp_form_v1' (UploadForm.tsx:64). PersistedForm (interface lines 82-94) holds targetTotalHm, ftp, nRiders, m, watchTarget, raceDate, startTime, stops, styrkortMaxRows, exposureTerrain, showInterval. saveToStorage (lines 106-112) writes JSON.stringify(data). gpxText is React state seeded from defaultRouteGpx (line 123) and is never written to localStorage; FIT is explicitly not persisted (comment line 122-126 'FIT is not persisted'). No file bytes/text are stored. The stored data is benign rider config; FTP and combined rider+bike mass persist across sessions and are mildly sensitive but acceptable for a local-only tool.

title: README 'web result and local result are identical' is misleading: CLI default uses fixed Vatternrundan controls, web uses generic controls
verdictReason: The underlying divergence is REAL, but the cited line is wrong and severity overstated. The 'identical' sentence is at README.md:5, not line 3 (line 3 is the route description). cli.ts soloControls returns the locked VATTERN_CONTROLS for non-solo (group) mode (cli.ts:226 'if (!cfg.solo) return VATTERN_CONTROLS;') while apps/web/src/lib/pipeline.ts builds Start+stops+finish controls, so the split/control table can differ for the same route. The pure physics/time-march IS identical, which is what most readers infer; this is a low-severity wording nuance, not a medium correctness bug.
evidence: README.md:5 'The same pure calculation core (@stp/core) runs in the browser app and the Node CLI, so the web result and the local result are identical.' packages/cli/src/cli.ts:226 'if (!cfg.solo) return VATTERN_CONTROLS;'; cli.ts:232 pushes a 'Mal' finish in solo mode. The control set therefore differs unless CLI runs --solo.
