title: Empty-string coercion: blank/missing lat or lon silently becomes 0 (Null Island), inflating route distance by 1000x with no error or NaN
evidence: Parser uses `lat: Number(pt['@_lat'])`. Because `Number('')===0` and `Number(null)===0` (verified: `Number("")`->0, `Number(" ")`->0, `Number(null)`->0), a single trkpt with `lat=""` parses to lat 0. Reproduced with a 5-point track (lat 58.00->58.04, lon 15) where point #3 has `lat=""`: parsed pts -> `[...,{"lat":0,"lon":15,...},...]`; ingestGpxString TOTAL route distance = 12,905,283 m vs CLEAN total = 4,448 m. The corrupted segment reports `dist=6450417 m` (a ~6450 km teleport to the equator and back) with NO throw, NO NaN (`NaN? false`), and grade clamped to a plausible ~1.5e-7. Input GPX at /tmp/fuzzgpx/batch4.mts.
recommendation: Validate coordinates after coercion: use a strict numeric parse (e.g. reject empty string before Number(), or use a regex/Number.isFinite check) and reject/skip points whose lat is not in [-90,90] or lon not in [-180,180], or throw a descriptive error. `Number('')` returning 0 is the trap; `parseFloat('')` returns NaN which would at least be detectable. Also note `Number('0x10')===16` and `Number('58,0')===NaN`, so locale/format variants mis-parse too.

title: Non-numeric / NaN / out-of-range coordinates accepted without validation, producing NaN-or-garbage segments and silently-empty plans
evidence: No range or finiteness check on parsed coords/ele. `out-of-range-coords` (lat="9999" lon="-9999" then lat="-1234" lon="5678") ingests to segs=1 cum_distance_m=6,163,379 m with no error. `non-numeric-latlon` (lat="north" lon="east", ele="abc") -> all NaN coords; dedupePoints then silently drops them because `haversine(...)>=0.5` is false for NaN, yielding segs=0 (an empty plan, no error). `literal-NaN-Infinity` (lat="NaN" lon="Infinity", lat="1e999"->Infinity) likewise -> segs=0. Reproduced in /tmp/fuzzgpx/harness.mts.
recommendation: After parse, assert every point has finite lat/lon in valid geographic range; treat ele NaN explicitly (e.g. default or reject). Make dedupePoints not silently swallow NaN-distance points (NaN comparisons are always false, so corrupt points vanish without trace). Surface a clear error or warning rather than emitting an empty/garbage segment array downstream to the solver.

title: Unbounded in-memory parse: no point-count or size cap; 3M-point (154MB) GPX consumes ~3.6GB RSS, a browser/serverless OOM-DoS vector
evidence: fast-xml-parser is non-streaming and the code maps the full point array with no cap. Measured (ingestGpxString, /tmp/fuzzgpx/batch3.mts): 100k pts=267MB/0.5s; 500k=870MB/2.8s; 1M (51MB xml)=1976MB/5.2s; 3M (154MB xml)=3645MB/19.7s RSS. The web app runs this in-browser on user-uploaded files (apps/web/src/components/UploadForm.tsx:344 `<input type="file" accept=".gpx,...">` -> App.tsx:77 / lib/pipeline.ts:170 `ingestGpxString(form.gpxText, cfg)`), so a crafted large GPX can OOM the user's tab.
recommendation: Cap input size and/or point count (reject files over e.g. a few hundred thousand points or N MB) before parsing, with a friendly error. Consider a streaming parser if huge legitimate routes are expected.

title: Uncaught TypeError on missing gpx/trk/trkseg/trkpt nodes (empty string, non-GPX XML, wrong namespace, empty trkseg)
evidence: parseGpxString does unchecked property access. Reproduced (/tmp/fuzzgpx/harness.mts): empty-string/whitespace-only/not-xml/no-gpx-element -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trk')` (doc['gpx'] is undefined, line 20-23); gpx-no-trk -> `...reading 'trkseg'` (line 27-30); gpx-trk-no-trkseg -> `...reading 'trkpt'` (line 34-37); gpx-empty-trkseg and self-closing `<trkseg/>` -> `...reading '@_lat'` (trkpt is undefined, mapped at line 44); namespaced-prefix (`<g:gpx>...`) -> `...reading 'trk'` (default-namespace mismatch). These crash instead of returning a clear 'invalid GPX' error.
recommendation: Guard each level (gpx/trk/trkseg/trkpt) and throw a single descriptive Error (e.g. 'Not a valid GPX file: missing <trk>/<trkseg>/<trkpt>'). The web App.tsx doFetch catch is bare `catch {}` -> generic error state with no message; pipeline run path should also fail gracefully.

title: Single-point and multi-trkseg GPX silently yield zero microsegments (empty plan) instead of an error
evidence: A valid single-trkpt file (`single-point`) ingests to segs=0 (buildMicroSegments loops `i < pts.length-1`, so 1 point -> 0 segments) with no error -> empty plan downstream. Also, when trk OR trkseg is an array, the code only keeps the FIRST (line 24-26 `trk = trk[0]`, line 31-33 `trkseg = trkseg[0]`): `multiple-trk-trkseg` (2 trkseg in trk1 + a second trk) ingests to segs=0 because only trkseg[0]'s single point survives. Real multi-segment routes silently lose all but the first segment. Reproduced in /tmp/fuzzgpx/harness.mts.
recommendation: Flatten all trk/trkseg into one point list rather than taking [0], and reject (or clearly warn on) routes with <2 usable points instead of emitting an empty segment array.

title: XXE external entities and billion-laughs are NOT exploitable with current parser config (defensive negative result)
evidence: XXE `<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">` -> fast-xml-parser throws `Error: External entities are not supported` (no file disclosure). Billion-laughs (9-level nested internal entities) and a 2^20 attribute-entity blowup do NOT expand: custom internal entities are left unexpanded, so `&i;`/`&big;` become non-numeric -> `Number(...)` -> NaN/0 (e.g. ele NaN; lat `&big;` -> lat null). No memory blowup, parse <2ms. Reproduced in /tmp/fuzzgpx/batch2.mts and batch3.mts. This is safe behavior by fast-xml-parser default and should not regress (e.g. if processEntities/DOCTYPE handling is later changed).
recommendation: No fix needed; keep the current XMLParser options (do not enable external entity / DTD expansion). Optionally add a regression test asserting external-entity GPX throws and that DOCTYPE entity values are not expanded into coordinates.

title: NaN/Infinity power sample propagates unguarded into np_w, np_target_candidate and exported plan.json anchor
evidence: analyzePass does no validation: `const np_w = normalizedPower(powerStream)` then `np_target_candidate = isLong ? Math.round(np_w) : Math.round(0.6 * cfg.ftp)`. Executed harness (tsx) on a long ride `[...Array(8000).fill(200), Infinity]`: observed `np_w=Infinity np_target_candidate=Infinity class=long_representative`. With one `NaN`: `np_w=NaN np_target_candidate=NaN`. With `-Infinity`: np_w=Infinity (v**4 positive). With huge values `1e300` (or even `1e80` summed over 8000 samples): meanFourthPow overflows to Infinity -> `np_w=Infinity`. normalizedPower has no isFinite guard; `meanFourthPow ** 0.25` propagates NaN/Infinity directly.
recommendation: Sanitize the stream before use: in readFitPowerBytes change the filter to `(p): p is number => typeof p === 'number' && Number.isFinite(p) && p >= 0`; and/or guard analyzePass/normalizedPower so np_w falls back (e.g. to 0.60*ftp) when not finite. A real Garmin FIT cannot carry these (power is uint16), but analyzePass/determineAnchorFromPower are exported public entry points fed arbitrary number[] (web worker, CLI).

title: Poisoned anchor silently serializes to null in plan.json (JSON.stringify(NaN|Infinity) === null)
evidence: buildPlanJson returns `{ config: cfg, anchor, ... }`. Web pipeline sets `cfg.np_target = anchor.np_target_candidate` (apps/web/src/lib/pipeline.ts:186) and `npTargetUsed = anchor.np_target_candidate` (line 187). Executed harness for an Infinity-poisoned long stream: `JSON.stringify(anchor)` => `{...,"mean_power_w":null,"np_w":null,...,"np_target_candidate":null,...}` and `JSON.stringify({np_target: cfg.np_target})` => `{"np_target":null}`. The note string still reads 'rolling NP Infinity W used directly as np_target', so note and numeric field disagree and the machine-readable artifact is corrupted with no error thrown.
recommendation: Validate the anchor (np_target_candidate / np_w / mean_power_w finite) before assigning cfg.np_target and before buildPlanJson; reject or fall back rather than emitting null. Fixing the root sanitization above resolves this downstream symptom too.

title: analyzePass with non-finite cfg.ftp yields NaN np_target_candidate on short_test path
evidence: Executed harness with `cfg({ ftp: NaN })` on a 100-sample stream: `np_target_candidate=NaN class=short_test`. The short/fallback path computes `Math.round(0.60 * cfg.ftp)` with no guard, so a NaN/Infinity ftp poisons the anchor (the no-FIT fallback in determineAnchorFromPower line 82 has the same issue). ftp defaults to 272 in applyDefaults, so this requires an explicitly bad ftp, hence low severity.
recommendation: Validate cfg.ftp is a finite positive number in applyDefaults (config.ts) and/or guard the 0.6*cfg.ftp computation so a malformed ftp cannot silently produce a NaN anchor.

title: readFitPowerBytes is robust to corrupt/empty/garbage/truncated bytes (no crash) - confirmed, not a bug
evidence: Executed harness with: empty Uint8Array, empty number[], 64 deterministic random bytes, 128 zero bytes, a faked valid 14-byte FIT header ('.FIT' magic) + 40 garbage bytes, and a valid SDK-encoded FIT truncated to half length. All returned `[]` (len 0) with no exception. Round-trip sanity (encode [100,200,300]) returned `[100,200,300]`. The @garmin/fitsdk Decoder swallows malformed/truncated data internally, so corrupt input degrades to an empty stream -> determineAnchorFromPower uses the 0.60*ftp fallback. Note: an empty/garbage FIT silently yields the FTP-fallback anchor rather than signalling the upload was unreadable.
recommendation: No fix required for crash-safety. Optional UX: distinguish 'no FIT' from 'FIT present but zero usable power records' so a corrupt/unreadable upload is surfaced instead of silently falling back to 0.60*ftp.

title: riderNpAtSpeed is non-monotone in v under strong tailwind+crosswind; bisection solver lands on a spurious slow root (more tailwind => slower plan, negative power, spinout cap bypassed)
evidence: REPRODUCED. Input: flat segment grade=0, bearing 90, wind 25 m/s FROM 250deg (apply_wind_height_correction:false) => headwind=-23.49, crosswind=8.55, npTarget=220. riderNpAtSpeed(v) rises to ~331W at v~8, falls to a minimum ~20W at v~20.5, then rises again (sampled: v=3.5->239, v=8.5->331, v=20.5->20, v=24.5->142). solveSpeedForRiderNp(220) returns v=3.093 m/s. Full runInnerSolve on a 1km segment gives v=3.00 m/s (10.8 km/h), cap_binding='none', p_pull_w=-317.9, p_mean_w=-213.6. Sweeping W at fixed NP: W=20 -> v=13.89 (spinout cap), then W=25 -> v=3.00 cap=none, W=30 -> v=1.78 cap=none: speed COLLAPSES as tailwind increases. The bisection comment claims 'riderNpAtSpeed is monotone increasing in v under normal conditions' (chaingang.ts:302) but it is not, so the root is wrong, the spinout ceiling (planner.ts:197-202) is never reached, and the negative-power clamp (planner.ts:221-224, spinout-only) does not fire.
recommendation: Do not assume monotonicity. The apparent-wind aero term F_aero=0.5*rho*CdA*v_app*u with v_app=hypot(u,cw) and u=v+headwind makes power non-monotone when u is large-negative (strong tailwind). Either (a) clamp/branch so the solver searches only the physically relevant (high-speed) root, e.g. seed lo at the speed where dP/dv>0 / start search above the minimum, (b) detect multiple roots and pick the largest, or (c) apply the spinout/vMax ceiling BEFORE solving and solve within [0.5, vMax] where the curve is better-behaved. Also clamp displayed p_pull_w/p_draft_w/p_mean_w to >=0 unconditionally, not only on cap_binding==='spinout'.

title: Negative pedal power leaks into SegmentPlan when cap_binding!=='spinout' (clamp is spinout-only)
evidence: REPRODUCED. Pure tailwind descent: grade=-0.06, bearing 90, wind 12 m/s FROM 270 (pure tailwind), npTarget=90, apply_wind_height_correction:false. runInnerSolve returns a segment with cap_binding='none', v=1.23 m/s, p_pull_w=-100.7, p_draft_w=-88.8, p_mean_w=-89.8. The clamp `if (cap_binding === 'spinout') { p_pull_w=Math.max(0,...); p_draft_w=Math.max(0,...) }` only runs for spinout segments, so any non-spinout segment whose steady power is negative (freewheel/tailwind, or the wrong-root case above) shows negative pedal power in the plan/tempokort.
recommendation: Clamp p_pull_w, p_draft_w and p_mean_w to >=0 for all segments (or document that negative = coasting). A race plan cannot show negative pedal effort.

title: Outer solver search range [60, cfg.ftp] is inverted when ftp<60; FTP below 60 is silently ignored and ftp=0 yields np_target_used=0
evidence: REPRODUCED. With ftp=0: solveForTargetTime returns np_target_used=0.000, total_s=22180, reachable=false (the 'fastest' pass runs runInnerSolve at hiNp=ftp=0, and since loNp=60>hiNp=0 bisection mid stays ~60..0 collapsed). With 0<ftp<60 (e.g. 30,50,59) the bisection collapses to np_used==ftp and IF pins to 1.000, ignoring the intended [60,ftp] sustainability band. The code comment (planner.ts:324) states 'Search range [60, cfg.ftp]' assuming ftp>=60.
recommendation: Guard ftp>=60 (or set loNp=Math.min(60,cfg.ftp)) and validate ftp>0 in applyDefaults. At minimum reject/normalize ftp<=0 so np_target_used can never be 0/negative.

title: NaN config fields propagate silently instead of erroring; ftp=NaN yields np_target_used=NaN, and m/crr/cda/eta=NaN pins speed to the 0.5 m/s solver floor
evidence: REPRODUCED. ftp=NaN: solveForTargetTime returns np_target_used=NaN (plan totals finite but the headline NP is NaN). m=NaN / crr=NaN / cda_pull=NaN / eta=NaN: pedalPower returns NaN, the bisection comparison `npMid<npTarget` is always false on NaN so hi=mid every iteration and solveSpeedForRiderNp collapses to v=0.5 (the lo floor) — segment speed is silently pinned to 0.5 m/s with no error (m=NaN trace: solveSpeedForRiderNp(150)=>v=0.5, np there=NaN, pullPower=NaN).
recommendation: Validate all numeric config fields are finite and in sane ranges in applyDefaults (throw a descriptive Error like the mandatory-field checks already do). NaN inputs should fail loudly, not produce a 0.5 m/s plan or a NaN NP.

title: n_riders=0 produces NaN rider-NP; negative pull_seconds / negative n_riders throw 'Invalid array length' from occupancyArray
evidence: REPRODUCED via riderNpAtSpeed(8,...) with crafted configs. n_riders=0,pull_seconds=45 => riderNp=NaN (solo=false, cycleLen=0, npMomentsFor divides by n=0). n_riders=2,pull_seconds=-10 => throws 'Invalid array length'. n_riders=-3,pull_seconds=45 => throws 'Invalid array length'. fFront(0,..)=1/0=Infinity is also unguarded.
recommendation: Validate n_riders>=1 (integer) and pull_seconds>=1 in applyDefaults; guard occupancyArray/npMomentsFor against non-positive cycle length.

title: pedalPower with eta=0 returns Infinity (unguarded divide by drivetrain efficiency)
evidence: REPRODUCED. pedalPower(8,0.05,0,{...eta:0}) => Infinity. eta is never validated >0; an eta=0 config would make every effort segment's power Infinity (and the solver would mis-behave).
recommendation: Validate 0<eta<=1 in applyDefaults, or guard the division.

title: airDensity returns Infinity/-Infinity for extreme/degenerate temperature inputs (T=0K, and Tetens singularity at tempC=-243.5 with humidity)
evidence: REPRODUCED. airDensity(-273.15,101325)=Infinity (T=0K => divide by zero). airDensity(-243.5,101325,0.6)=-Infinity (Tetens es denominator (T-29.65)->0 at T=29.65K i.e. tempC=-243.5, plus virtual-temp term goes negative). These are far outside race conditions but are unvalidated and would silently poison rho if a weather source ever returned a junk temperature.
recommendation: Clamp/validate temperature to a plausible range (e.g. -60..60 C) before computing density, or guard the denominators. Low priority given real weather inputs, but it is an unguarded Inf source feeding the physics.

title: Uncaught TypeError when pts is a non-string single value (number/boolean/object) instead of 400
evidence: Executed via tsx with fetch mocked. Inputs {date:'2026-06-13', pts:5814}, {pts:true}, {pts:{}} each threw: "TypeError: pts.split is not a function or its return value is not iterable\n    at parseWeatherQuery (/Users/tim/StickToThePlan/api/handler.ts:45:26)\n    at handleWeather (.../handler.ts:61:18)". Root cause: line 34-36 first() only unwraps Array; a non-string scalar passes through, then line 45 `pts.split('|')` throws. handleWeather has no try/catch, so it rejects the promise instead of returning {status:400}. NOTE: not reachable via the deployed Vercel adapter (weather.ts line 6 casts req.query whose type is `{[key:string]: string | string[]}`, so pts is always string|string[]). It IS reachable for any direct caller of the exported parseWeatherQuery/handleWeather, which handler.ts top comment advertises as 'Pure-ish ... decoupled from the Vercel runtime so it can be unit-tested'.
recommendation: In first()/parseWeatherQuery, guard that the unwrapped date and pts are typeof 'string' before use (e.g. `if (typeof date !== 'string' || typeof pts !== 'string') return null;`). This makes the pure function honor its null-on-invalid contract instead of throwing.

title: Uncaught TypeError when the query object itself is null or undefined
evidence: Executed via tsx. handleWeather(null) threw "TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'date')" and handleWeather(undefined) threw "...of undefined (reading 'date')", both at parseWeatherQuery (.../handler.ts:40:24) where it does `const date = first(q.date)`. No try/catch in handleWeather (line 60-76) so the promise rejects rather than returning a 400. NOT reachable via Vercel adapter (req.query is always a non-null object), but breaks the exported pure-function contract used by api/tests.
recommendation: Treat a missing/non-object query as invalid: `if (!q || typeof q !== 'object') return null;` at the top of parseWeatherQuery. Optionally wrap handleWeather body in try/catch returning 400 as defense in depth.

title: Number() coercion accepts hex, scientific, padded, and whitespace coordinate strings (no NaN/crash, but silently mis-parses)
evidence: Executed via tsx, parseWeatherQuery returned (not null) for: pts='0x10,0x20' => {lat:16,lon:32}; pts='5e1,1e1' => {lat:50,lon:10}; pts=' 58.5 , 14.6 ' => {lat:58.5,lon:14.6}; pts='   ,14.6' => {lat:0,lon:14.6} (whitespace-only latS is truthy so the line-49 empty-half guard misses it, then Number('   ')===0). All produce in-range finite coords, so they 200 and forward only clean re-serialized String(Number) URLs (e.g. latitude=16&longitude=32) to api.open-meteo.com. No crash, no upstream taint, no injection. Pure data-quality looseness: `Number()` is more permissive than a strict decimal-coordinate parse.
recommendation: If strict coordinates are desired, validate each half against a decimal regex (e.g. /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/) and trim before Number(), and reject whitespace-only halves. Low priority: current behavior is safe (bounded + re-serialized), only cosmetically permissive.

title: Semantically-impossible but regex-valid dates (9999-99-99, 0000-00-00) pass validation and are forwarded upstream
evidence: Executed via tsx. ISO_DATE = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ only checks shape, not calendar validity. Inputs date='9999-99-99' and date='0000-00-00' (with pts='58.5,14.6') returned status 200 and forwarded 4 upstream URLs containing start_date=9999-99-99 / 0000-00-00. These are passed verbatim to Open-Meteo (which will reject them upstream and the fetch-error path returns []). No crash, no SSRF (host is fixed), but a nonsense date reaches the third-party API instead of being rejected at the edge.
recommendation: Optionally validate the date is a real calendar date and within an accepted forecast window (e.g. parse with Date and re-compare, or bound month 01-12 / day 01-31) before fetching, to fail fast at 400 rather than relying on the upstream to reject.

title: Confirmed: injection chars, CRLF, out-of-range coords, oversized payloads, and unicode all 400 safely and forward nothing
evidence: Executed via tsx across the corpus, fetch mocked to record forwarded URLs. All of these returned status 400 with forwarded=0 (no upstream call) and body {error}: CRLF header-injection pts '58.5,14.6\r\nHost: evil'; URL-param injection '58.5,14.6&evil=1'; '?foo=bar'; sql-ish date "2026-06-13'; DROP"; out-of-range '100,14.6'/'58.5,200'/'-91,14.6'/'58.5,-181'/'90.0000001,14.6'/'1e300,1e300'; Infinity/-Infinity/NaN; over-cap 65 and 10000 points; 1MB pipes and 5MB garbage strings; unicode emoji and fullwidth digits; embedded null byte; empty-half ',14.6' and '58.5,'; date array whose first element is invalid. Boundary coords 90,180 and -90,-180 correctly 200 (inclusive bounds per line 53). Zero TAINTED-FORWARD findings: every URL that was built used the fixed api.open-meteo.com / ensemble-api.open-meteo.com hosts with String(Number)-serialized coords, so no raw attacker text reached an upstream URL.
recommendation: No action; documents that the string-path validation (the externally-reachable surface) is sound. The only real fixes are the two non-string/null type-safety crashes above.

title: Non-numeric / comma-decimal lat-lon-ele silently coerced to NaN (locale GPX corrupts route with no error)
evidence: parseGpxString does `lat: Number(pt['@_lat'])` etc. with no validation. REPRODUCED: input `<trkpt lat="58,123" lon="14,456"><ele>100,5</ele></trkpt>` (European comma-decimal, emitted by many GPS tools) -> parseGpxString returns {lat:NaN,lon:NaN,ele:NaN}; harness printed `all lat NaN? true all ele NaN? true`. Same for any junk: `lat="abc"`, `lat="NaN"`, `lat="Infinity"` all become NaN. No exception is thrown, so the bad route flows downstream.
recommendation: After Number() coercion, validate each point: reject/throw on NaN/Infinity and on lat outside [-90,90] / lon outside [-180,180]. Optionally accept comma-decimals by normalizing. Surface a clear 'invalid GPX coordinate' error instead of producing NaN.

title: NaN coordinate collapses the entire route to 0 microsegments, then segment() crashes downstream
evidence: dedupePoints keeps a point only when `haversine(prev,cur) >= 0.5`. With a NaN coordinate, haversine returns NaN and `NaN >= 0.5` is always false, so every following point is dropped. REPRODUCED: 4-point input with NaN first point -> `dedupePoints` returns 1 point; full ingest of `<trkpt lat="bad" lon="bad">...<trkpt lat="58.1" lon="14.1">` yields `micros=0`. Feeding those 0 micros into segment() (the real CLI/web path) THREW: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')`. So one bad coordinate (e.g. the very common comma-decimal first point) silently destroys the route and then hard-crashes the planner.
recommendation: Filter NaN coords before dedupe (or validate at parse). Guard dedupePoints against NaN distances. Make segment()/planner tolerate an empty micro array (throw a clear 'GPX produced no usable points' error) instead of dereferencing undefined.

title: Valid GPX route/waypoint files (<rte>/<rtept>, <wpt>) crash the parser
category: unhandled exception / cryptic error on valid input
evidence: parseGpxString only reads gpx.trk -> trkseg -> trkpt; it ignores <rte>/<rtept> and <wpt>. REPRODUCED: a valid GPX 1.1 route `<gpx version="1.1"><rte><rtept lat="58.0" lon="14.0">...</rte></gpx>` -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trkseg')`. Waypoint-only file `<gpx><wpt lat=...></wpt></gpx>` -> same throw. These are standard GPX documents commonly exported by route planners (Komoot/RideWithGPS/etc.); the web UI's file upload (UploadForm.tsx:344 accepts .gpx) feeds them straight into ingestGpxString.
recommendation: Fall back to <rte>/<rtept> (and optionally <wpt>) when no <trk> is present, or throw a clear 'GPX contains no track (trk); route/waypoint-only files are not supported' message instead of a property-access TypeError.

title: Hard-coded trk[0]/trkseg[0] crashes on multi-segment/multi-track GPX whose first seg is empty
evidence: `if (Array.isArray(trk)) trk = trk[0]` and the same for trkseg always pick index 0 and discard the rest. REPRODUCED: `<trk><trkseg></trkseg><trkseg><trkpt .../></trkseg></trk>` (points only in the 2nd segment) -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '@_lat')`. `<trk></trk><trk>...points...</trk>` (points only in 2nd track) -> `TypeError: ...(reading 'trkpt')`. Garmin/Strava devices routinely emit multiple <trkseg> across pause/resume, and an empty leading segment is a common artifact, so real recordings can hit this.
recommendation: Iterate and concatenate trkpt across all <trk> and all <trkseg> rather than only [0]; skip empty segments.

title: Empty / non-track / non-XML input throws raw TypeError (no input guard)
evidence: No null/shape checks after parser.parse. REPRODUCED throws: empty string '' -> `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trk')`; `<gpx/>` (self-closing) -> `(reading 'trkseg')`; `<gpx><trk><trkseg></trkseg></trk></gpx>` (empty trkseg) -> `(reading '@_lat')` (because non-array undefined trkpt is wrapped into `[undefined]` at line 38-40); JSON `{...}` and an HTML 404 page both -> `(reading 'trk')`; namespaced `<g:gpx>...` -> `(reading 'trk')`. These are exactly the inputs a paste/upload box or a server returning an error page will produce. In the web app these reach runPipeline (pipeline.ts:170) and surface only as a cryptic internal message via the worker error channel (solve.worker.ts:27-30).
recommendation: Validate doc.gpx, trk, trkseg, and trkpt presence and throw descriptive domain errors (e.g. 'Not a GPX file', 'GPX has no track points'). Filter the `[undefined]` case at line 38-40 (`if (!Array.isArray(trkpts)) trkpts = trkpts == null ? [] : [trkpts]`).

title: Non-numeric <ele> with valid coords yields grade=NaN for every segment (silent), smoothing spreads one bad value
evidence: REPRODUCED: coords valid but `<ele>n/a</ele>` on the first point -> ingest returns 2 micros with `ele_start NaN? [true,true]` and `grade= [NaN, NaN]`. smoothElevation propagates the NaN to neighbors (centered average), and buildMicroSegments computes `(eleEnd-eleStart)/distance_m` = NaN; the Math.max/Math.min clamp does not sanitize NaN. These NaN grades flow into the physics/planner producing NaN speeds and ETAs with no error.
recommendation: Default a missing/non-numeric <ele> to 0 (or carry-forward) and validate; or guard grade so NaN -> 0. At minimum reject NaN elevations at parse time.

title: buildCourseGpx throws when cfg.stops is undefined (applyDefaults never sets stops)
category: unhandled exception (adjacent to GPX output path)
evidence: `for (const stop of cfg.stops)` is unguarded; applyDefaults (config.ts:91-101) never defaults `stops`, so `applyDefaults({gpx_path,race_date,start_time}).stops === undefined` (verified). REPRODUCED via course output: `TypeError: cfg.stops is not iterable`. Triggered whenever a config omits stops (the web pipeline passes form.stops which may be undefined).
recommendation: Default stops to [] in applyDefaults, or guard `for (const stop of cfg.stops ?? [])` in buildCourseGpx.

title: NEGATIVE RESULT: XXE external entities are blocked; nested DTD entities are NOT expanded (no billion-laughs DoS)
evidence: fast-xml-parser 5.8.0 with the config in gpx.ts. REPRODUCED: `<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">` -> parser throws `Error: External entities are not supported` (no file read). Classic 7-level billion-laughs measured: the top entity's expanded text length stayed at 3 chars (literal `&g;`) for depths 4..8, i.e. nested entities are NOT recursively expanded; parse stayed at 89MB RSS / <3ms. So XXE and entity-expansion DoS are not exploitable through this parser config. Reported for completeness.
recommendation: No action needed for XXE/entity expansion. Keep relying on the parser's defaults; do not enable processEntities for external/DTD entities if the config is ever changed.

title: NEGATIVE/PERF: 1M trkpt parses (no crash) but uses ~1.3GB RSS for a 56MB input (~23x); deep nesting is capped
evidence: REPRODUCED: generated 1,000,000-point GPX (56MB) -> ingestGpxString returned 999,999 micros in 4.3s using rss=1295MB (needed --max-old-space-size=2048; default heap would OOM on a larger file). Deeply nested elements (10k <x> levels) are rejected by the parser: `Error: Maximum nested tags exceeded` (clean throw, no hang). So very large but well-formed GPX is a memory-amplification concern (no size/point cap before parsing) but not a parser crash; depth bombs are handled.
recommendation: Add an input size cap and/or a max-point cap before/after parsing (the web upload accepts arbitrary files). Consider rejecting GPX above a sane byte/point threshold to avoid OOM on hostile uploads.

title: Single NaN power sample in a long ride makes np_target_candidate NaN (no validation, serializes to null in plan.json)
evidence: Reproduced: analyzePass(stream, cfg) on a 7300-sample stream with one NaN (long_representative branch) -> np_w=NaN, np_target_candidate=NaN, mean_power_w=NaN. Root cause: `const np_w = normalizedPower(powerStream)` and normalizedPower returns NaN if any sample is NaN (`rolling.reduce((a,v)=>a+v**4) ... ** 0.25` -> NaN), then line 46 `Math.round(np_w)` = NaN. JSON.stringify of the anchor produced: `"np_w":null,..."np_target_candidate":null` and the note literally reads 'rolling NP NaN W used directly as np_target'. readFitPowerBytes does NOT filter NaN: its filter is only `typeof p === 'number'`, and `typeof NaN === 'number'` is true, so NaN survives.
recommendation: In readFitPowerBytes, tighten the filter to `Number.isFinite(p)` instead of `typeof p === 'number'` so NaN/Infinity records are dropped. Additionally guard normalizedPower / analyzePass to reject or skip non-finite samples and assert np_w is finite before using it as np_target_candidate.

title: Negative or out-of-range power in a valid FIT wraps via uint16 encoding to absurd values, inflating np_target ~3x with no sanity check
evidence: Reproduced end-to-end via the real @garmin/fitsdk Encoder->readFitPowerBytes->analyzePass. A long ride (7300 samples @ 180 W) with ONE glitch sample of -5 W (common power-meter dropout) decodes through the uint16 `power` field as 65531 W. Result: classification=long_representative, np_w=598.34, np_target_candidate=598 W, note='rolling NP 598 W used directly as np_target'. True NP ~180 W, so the headline anchor is inflated 3.3x. Also reproduced: power -200 -> decodes 65336; power 70000 -> 4464 (mod 65536); power 1e9 -> 51712. None are rejected; all flow into mean_power_w / np_w / np_target_candidate.
recommendation: After decoding, clamp/validate power samples to a physically plausible range (e.g. drop or warn on values <0 or > ~2000 W) before passing to analyzePass. Add a sanity assertion on np_target_candidate (e.g. cap at a multiple of cfg.ftp) and surface a warning note instead of silently using an impossible anchor.

title: solveSpeedForRiderNp(NaN) silently returns lower bound 0.5 m/s instead of erroring
evidence: Reproduced: solveSpeedForRiderNp(NaN, 0,0,0,1.2,cfg) returns v=0.5 (not NaN, no throw). Cause: with npTarget=NaN, `Math.abs(npMid - NaN) < 0.1` is always false and `npMid < NaN` is always false, so the else branch runs every iteration (hi=mid), collapsing toward lo=0.5; after 60 iters returns (lo+hi)/2 ~= 0.5. solveSpeedForRiderNp(Infinity) and (1e9) likewise return 0.5. A NaN/garbage anchor reaching this solver yields a plausible-looking 0.5 m/s (1.8 km/h) ground speed silently rather than failing fast. (Note: in the current pipeline the outer solver bisects np in [60, cfg.ftp] independently of cfg.np_target, so today the NaN anchor poisons reported metadata, not this call; but the solver itself has no NaN guard and would mis-converge if ever called with a non-finite target.)
recommendation: Guard solveSpeedForRiderNp: if `!Number.isFinite(npTarget)` throw or return NaN explicitly rather than degenerating to the lower bound. Optionally track whether convergence actually occurred (tolerance met) vs. running out of iterations.

title: Negative power stream yields a positive NP (sign lost via fourth power)
evidence: Reproduced: analyzePass([-300,-300,-300,-300,-300], cfg) -> mean_power_w=-300 but np_w=300. normalizedPower computes mean(rolling^4)^0.25, and (-300)^4 is positive, so the fourth root returns +300. A fully-negative (corrupt) power stream is silently reported as a valid positive NP while mean_power_w stays negative, an internally inconsistent FitPassMetrics.
recommendation: Reject or zero-clamp negative power samples in readFitPowerBytes/analyzePass before NP computation, so np_w cannot mask a physically invalid (negative) stream.

title: Huge/Infinity power flows into np_target as Infinity and serializes to null in plan.json
evidence: Reproduced: analyzePass(Array(7300).fill(1e308)) -> np_w=Infinity, np_target_candidate=Infinity, mean_power_w=Infinity; JSON round-trip turns each into null in the anchor block embedded by buildPlanJson (planJson.ts line 86 spreads `anchor` directly). 1e155 inputs already overflow to Infinity at the `v**4` step (mean fourth power exceeds Number.MAX_VALUE). The note text reads 'rolling NP Infinity W used directly as np_target'. No finiteness check before serialization.
recommendation: Same fix as finding 1/2: drop non-finite samples at ingest and assert finite np_w before building FitPassMetrics, so plan.json never contains null/Infinity for the anchor.

title: readFitPowerBytes never throws on corrupt/garbage/empty FIT bytes (silent empty result)
evidence: Reproduced: readFitPowerBytes returns [] for empty Uint8Array, empty array, 64 bytes of deterministic 'random' data, 128 bytes of 0xff, and a valid-looking 14-byte FIT header followed by 64 garbage bytes. No throw in any case. The empty stream then flows to analyzePass which returns the short_test 0.60*ftp fallback (np_target_candidate=150 for ftp=250), so a corrupt upload is silently treated as 'no usable power' rather than reported as an error to the user.
recommendation: Distinguish 'decoder failed / produced zero records from non-empty bytes' from 'legitimately empty file' and surface a warning (or throw) so a corrupt upload is not silently downgraded to the FTP-fallback anchor without the user knowing.

title: NaN target_total_hm silently produces a bogus "reachable" plan instead of an error
evidence: hmToSeconds('abc') / '' / '11:xx' all return NaN (time.ts:10-13: `h*3600+m*60` with Number('abc')=NaN). In solveForTargetTime `const target = hmToSeconds(...)` becomes NaN. The guard `if (fastest.total_time_s > target)` is false (any compare with NaN is false), so the unreachable branch is skipped; in the bisect loop both `Math.abs(total - NaN) <= 20` and `total > NaN` are false, so `hi = mid` every iteration and np collapses to lo=60. Observed: target_total_hm='abc' -> total=1621s, np=60, reachable=true (a 0:00 target correctly returns reachable=false, so behavior is inconsistent and silently wrong for malformed strings).
recommendation: Validate target_total_hm (and reject NaN/non-finite) in applyDefaults or at the top of solveForTargetTime; throw or clamp. Make hmToSeconds throw on unparseable input rather than returning NaN.

title: riderNpAtSpeed is non-monotone under tailwind; solveSpeedForRiderNp bisection returns wrong-branch speed exceeding tolerance
evidence: solveSpeedForRiderNp comment asserts 'riderNpAtSpeed is monotone increasing in v under normal conditions', but under tailwind the apparent wind u=v+headwind reverses sign so the NP curve has a dip (e.g. tw=-12 m/s, n_riders=12, rho=1.2: NP at v=1..7 = 16,25,28,26,21,13,5 then rises again 8,9->15,26). For npTarget=6 W the bisection returns v=0.5 (bracket floor) with actual NP=8.94 W: err 2.94 W against the documented 0.1 W tolerance, and 6 W is genuinely reachable near v=7.x. Reproduced directly: `solveSpeedForRiderNp(6,0,-12,0,1.2,cfg)` -> v=0.5, NP=8.94.
recommendation: Either prove/enforce monotonicity over the searched bracket, restrict the bisection to the rising right branch (search downward from v=25 for the highest root, matching 'plan the fastest sustainable speed'), or switch to a bracketing root-finder that handles the dip. At minimum detect non-convergence (|np-target|>tol after the loop) and flag it.

title: Negative stop.minutes produce negative ETAs and negative total_time_s (finish-before-start)
evidence: `const addS = stop.minutes * 60;` is added unconditionally with no lower bound. With stops=[{control:'X',km:5,minutes:-100}] on a 20km route: solveForTargetTime returns total_time_s=-2758.7, stop_time_s=-6000, stops[0].depart_s=-5189.7, and the final segment eta_s=-2758.7 (an ETA before the race start). These negative ETAs flow into tempokort/FIT/course exports unguarded.
recommendation: Clamp stop.minutes to >=0 (or validate in applyDefaults) before multiplying by 60; reject negative stop durations.

title: n_riders=0 yields fFront=1/0=Infinity and NaN p_mean_w across the whole plan
evidence: fFront(0,..) hits `return 1/nRiders` = Infinity (only nRiders===1 is special-cased). meanPower(pull,draft,Infinity) = Infinity*pull + (1-Infinity)*draft = NaN. runInnerSolve(route(5),200,calm,cfg({n_riders:0})) -> every segment's p_mean_w = NaN. applyDefaults only derives solo from `n_riders===1` and never validates n_riders>=1, so 0 (or negative) passes straight through.
recommendation: Validate n_riders is an integer >=1 in applyDefaults; guard fFront against nRiders<=0.

title: airDensity returns negative/Infinite density for sub-absolute-zero temperature, feeding negative drag into the solver
evidence: airDensity(-273.15,101325)=Infinity (T=0 K -> divide by zero) and airDensity(-300,101325)=-13.146 (negative T in kelvin -> negative rho). A WeatherFn returning temp_c=-300 makes runInnerSolve produce rho=-13.146 and p_pull_w=-293.1 (negative aero drag) with no error. Pressure_pa=0 gives rho=0 (no drag). No clamp on the kelvin temperature or returned density.
recommendation: Clamp T to a small positive kelvin floor (or reject temp_c<=-273.15) and assert rho>0; physically out-of-range weather should be rejected, not silently produce negative drag.

title: No validation of mass m / eta / ftp; m<=0, eta=0, ftp<=0 produce nonsensical-but-non-erroring plans
evidence: applyDefaults validates only gpx_path/race_date/start_time. Observed: m=0 -> plan finishes (zero gravity+rolling terms, only aero) reachable=true; m=-96 -> total=292min reachable=true (negative gravity assists/opposes nonsensically). eta=0 -> pedalPower divides by 0 (P=pWheel/eta) so power=Infinity, every effort segment is hard-capped to v=0.5, total pinned. ftp<=0 -> outer bracket [60, ftp] is inverted (hi<lo); solver still returns np~60. ftp=1e9 -> intensity_factor=6e-8 (meaningless). None raise an error.
recommendation: In applyDefaults assert m>0, 0<eta<=1, ftp>0 (and ftp>=60 so the [60,ftp] bracket is valid), throwing descriptive errors like the existing mandatory-field checks.

title: Zero-length microsegment gives time_s=0 (0/v) but speedAtPull/solver still runs; division-by-v guarded only by v>=0.5
evidence: A microsegment with distance_m=0 yields time_s = 0/v = 0 cleanly (v floored at 0.5 by the solvers), so no NaN; runInnerSolve(route(1,0),...) -> time_s=0, total=0. Not a defect by itself, but combined with an all-zero-length / empty route the plan reports total_time_s=0, rider_np_ride_w=0, intensity_factor=0, reachable=true (solveForTargetTime([]) returns np_target_used=60, total=0, reachable=true) which a caller may misinterpret as a valid instant-finish plan.
recommendation: Consider rejecting empty/zero-distance routes (no effort segments) with reachable=false or an explicit note rather than returning a 0s 'reachable' plan.

title: Non-string pts crashes handler with uncaught TypeError -> 500 instead of safe 400
evidence: first() does `return Array.isArray(v) ? v[0] : v;` (line 34-36) which only unwraps ONE array level, and parseWeatherQuery then does `for (const pair of pts.split('|'))` (line 45) with no typeof guard. Executed via tsx: handleWeather({date:'2026-06-13', pts:{}}) , pts:42, pts:true, and pts:[[...]] / pts:[42] all THREW `TypeError: pts.split is not a function`. weather.ts:4-9 calls `await handleWeather(...)` with NO try/catch, so the rejection escapes -> Vercel FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED (500), not the intended 400. Observed: 'pts=42 (number): handleWeather THREW TypeError' and 'pts=[42] array w/ number -> THREW pts.split is not a function'.
recommendation: Guard the type before splitting: in first() or parseWeatherQuery, treat any non-string date/pts as invalid (e.g. `if (typeof pts !== 'string') return null;`). Also wrap the handleWeather call in api/weather.ts in try/catch returning 400/500 JSON so no input can produce an unhandled rejection.

title: ISO_DATE regex accepts semantically invalid dates, forwarded verbatim into upstream URLs
evidence: `const ISO_DATE = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/;` (line 26) validates shape only, not calendar validity. Executed via tsx: handleWeather({date:'9999-99-99'|'2026-13-40'|'0000-00-00', pts:'58.5,14.6'}) all returned parse=ACCEPT, status=200, and issued 4 upstream fetches. buildForecastUrl(...,'2026-13-40') produced `...&start_date=2026-13-40&end_date=2026-13-40...` (openMeteo.ts:33-44) — the bogus month/day 13/40 is sent straight to api.open-meteo.com. So bad data IS forwarded upstream rather than rejected.
recommendation: After the regex, validate the date is a real calendar date and within an allowed window (e.g. parse with Date and confirm round-trip, plus reject far-past/future). Reject 9999-99-99, 2026-13-40, 0000-00-00 with 400 instead of forwarding them to upstream APIs.

title: Number() coercion silently accepts hex, exponential, and whitespace-padded coordinates
evidence: `const lat = Number(latS), lon = Number(lonS);` then only checks Number.isFinite + range (lines 50-53). Number() accepts non-decimal forms. Executed via tsx: pts='0x2D,0x10' parsed to {lat:45,lon:16}; pts='5.85e1,1.46e1' parsed to {lat:58.5,lon:14.6}; pts='  58.5\t,\n14.6  ' (leading/trailing whitespace+tabs+newlines) parsed to {lat:58.5,lon:14.6}. These non-canonical inputs are accepted and forwarded as valid coordinates instead of being rejected as malformed.
recommendation: Validate each half against a strict decimal pattern (e.g. /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/ after trim, or reject if it contains x/e/whitespace) before Number(), so only well-formed decimal coordinates are accepted. Low impact (values stay in range) but it accepts ill-formed client input the contract implies should be rejected.

title: ISO_DATE regex is not ReDoS-vulnerable (negative result, verified)
evidence: Ran parseWeatherQuery with date = '9'.repeat(2_000_000)+'-06-13'; parse completed in ~0.2ms and returned null (rejected). The anchored fixed-length pattern /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ has no catastrophic backtracking. Reported as a non-issue to document the fuzz coverage.
recommendation: No action needed; included to record that the regex DoS vector was tested and is safe.

title: NaN coordinate in any kept point silently discards the entire rest of the route via dedupePoints
evidence: parseGpxString does `lat: Number(pt['@_lat'])` with no validation, so a non-numeric/missing lat yields lat=NaN. In dedupePoints the guard is `if (dist >= 0.5)`; with a NaN-coordinate kept point, `haversine(NaN, valid)=NaN` and `NaN >= 0.5` is `false`, so EVERY subsequent point is dropped. REPRODUCED: GPX with 1001 trkpts where only the FIRST has lat="bad" -> `deduped to 1 pts (rest silently discarded)` -> `microsegments produced: 0 (expected ~1000)`. Same with lat="Infinity" first: 3 parsed -> 0 segments. No error is thrown; the planner just gets an empty/near-empty route.
recommendation: Validate parsed lat/lon/ele in parseGpxString: reject (throw) or skip points where Number(...) is NaN/non-finite or out of [-90,90]/[-180,180]. In dedupePoints, treat a NaN distance as 'not a duplicate' (keep the point) or guard against NaN coordinates explicitly so a single bad point cannot annihilate the route.

title: Large GPX (>~1M points / 60MB) drives the pipeline to multi-second freeze and JS heap OOM with no size cap
evidence: ingestGpxString holds the full XML string + fast-xml-parser DOM + RoutePoint[] + smoothed number[] + MicroSegment[] all live, with no point/byte cap. REPRODUCED under `--max-old-space-size=2048`: N=100000 (6MB) -> 419ms/152MB; N=1000000 (60.5MB) -> 4003ms/1167MB; building N=3000000 -> `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`. This runs on the browser main thread in App.tsx doFetch (line 77) and in the web worker via runPipeline (apps/web/src/lib/pipeline.ts:170), where a user can paste/upload an arbitrarily large .gpx (UploadForm.tsx:344). A 60MB GPX is well within plausible upload size and already costs ~1.2GB, freezing/crashing the tab.
recommendation: Enforce an input cap before parsing (max bytes and/or max trkpt count) and reject oversized GPX with a clear error. Consider streaming/incremental parsing for very large tracks, and run ingest off the main thread for the synchronous App.tsx path.

title: Malformed/empty GPX throws raw internal TypeErrors instead of a validated GPX error
evidence: No structural validation: `const gpx = doc['gpx']` then `gpx['trk']` etc. REPRODUCED: empty string and `<foo/>` -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trk')`; `<gpx></gpx>` -> `...(reading 'trkseg')`; `<gpx><trk><trkseg></trkseg></trk></gpx>` and the full ingestGpxString on a 0-point trkseg -> `...(reading '@_lat')` (because empty trkseg makes trkpts=[undefined] then `.map` reads @_lat of undefined). Wrong namespace `<gpx:gpx ...>` -> `...(reading 'trk')`. These bubble up as generic TypeErrors; App.tsx:87 swallows them into an opaque 'error' state with no actionable message, and any non-try/catch caller crashes.
recommendation: After parse, validate presence of gpx/trk/trkseg and that trkpt resolves to a non-empty array; throw a descriptive domain error (e.g. 'GPX contains no track points'). Filter out undefined entries before .map so an empty <trkseg></trkseg> yields 0 points rather than a TypeError.

title: Missing <ele> on points produces NaN grade/elevation in every microsegment, silently corrupting the plan
evidence: `ele: Number(pt['ele'])` is NaN when <ele> is absent or non-numeric. smoothElevation sums NaN -> NaN, and grade `(eleEnd - eleStart) / distance_m` stays NaN (Math.max/min with NaN returns NaN). REPRODUCED: GPX with three trkpts and NO <ele> -> every microsegment `grade=NaN ele=NaN->NaN`. Also `ele=high` (non-numeric) and `<ele>NaN</ele>` yield ele=NaN. These NaNs flow downstream into the pacing/grade model with no error.
recommendation: Default a missing/invalid <ele> to a sane value (e.g. 0 or previous point's ele) or reject the file; clamp/guard grade so NaN cannot propagate (e.g. treat NaN elevation delta as 0 grade).

title: Multi-trk / multi-trkseg GPX silently keeps only the first segment, dropping the rest of the route
evidence: `if (Array.isArray(trk)) { trk = trk[0]; }` and the same for trkseg: only the FIRST track and FIRST segment are ever read. REPRODUCED: GPX with 2 trks / 2 trksegs totalling 5 trkpts -> `parsed 2 pts (only first trkseg read; 3 points silently lost)`. Real-world GPX exports frequently split a route across multiple <trkseg> (e.g. after pauses) or multiple <trk>; the tail of the route silently vanishes with no warning, producing a plan for a truncated route.
recommendation: Concatenate trkpts across all trk and all trkseg elements (flatMap) instead of taking index [0], or at minimum warn/throw when more than one segment/track is present and only the first is used.

title: Duplicate or structured <ele> child coerces to NaN elevation
evidence: `ele: Number(pt['ele'])` assumes <ele> is a scalar. When a trkpt has two <ele> tags, fast-xml-parser returns an array, and `Number([10,20])` is NaN. REPRODUCED: `<trkpt ...><ele>10</ele><ele>20</ele></trkpt>` -> `ele=NaN`. Same coercion-to-NaN would occur if <ele> parses to an object. This NaN then feeds smoothElevation/grade as in the missing-ele finding.
recommendation: Coerce ele defensively: if pt['ele'] is an array/object, take the first scalar (or reject); validate the result is finite before use.

title: XXE external-entity and billion-laughs amplification are NOT exploitable with fast-xml-parser v5 defaults (negative result)
evidence: REPRODUCED to confirm safety: XXE `<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">` -> `Error: External entities are not supported` (thrown by the library, no file read). Billion-laughs / nested internal-entity expansion at depths 3,5,7,9 (theoretical 1e4..1e10 chars) produced no amplification (heapDelta ~0MB, <3ms) and left the value unexpanded (Number(ele)=NaN). fast-xml-parser v5.8.0 (pinned in packages/core/package.json) does not resolve nested internal entities or external entities by default.
recommendation: No action required for XXE/billion-laughs, but pin fast-xml-parser (avoid passing processEntities/custom entity options) so this safe default is not regressed; add a regression test asserting external entities throw.

title: readFitPowerBytes type filter admits NaN/Infinity (no Number.isFinite check)
evidence: `.filter((p): p is number => typeof p === 'number')` — typeof NaN === 'number' and typeof Infinity === 'number', so non-finite power survives. Reproduced: `analyzePass(Array(10).fill(NaN), cfg)` -> {mean_power_w: NaN, np_w: NaN}; `analyzePass(Array(10).fill(Infinity), cfg)` -> {np_w: Infinity}.
recommendation: Change the predicate to `(p): p is number => typeof p === 'number' && Number.isFinite(p)` so NaN/±Infinity records are dropped exactly like null/undefined.

title: NaN/Infinity power propagates into np_target_candidate for long rides
evidence: For duration_s>7200 the anchor is `np_target_candidate = Math.round(np_w)` with no finite-guard. Reproduced via direct execution: `analyzePass(Array(7201).fill(NaN), cfg)` -> np_target_candidate: NaN; `analyzePass(Array(7201).fill(1e200), cfg)` -> np_target_candidate: Infinity; `determineAnchorFromPower(Array(7201).fill(NaN), cfg)` -> np_target_candidate: NaN. The accompanying note prints 'rolling NP NaN W used directly as np_target'.
recommendation: After computing np_w in analyzePass, guard: if !Number.isFinite(np_w) treat as the FTP-fallback path (or throw a descriptive error). Never let a non-finite np_w become np_target_candidate.

title: Corrupt anchor (Infinity/NaN) silently serializes to null in downloadable plan.json
evidence: buildPlanJson embeds the FitPassMetrics anchor verbatim (`anchor,`). Reproduced: with a long Infinity-power anchor, JSON.stringify(buildPlanJson(...)) emits `"anchor":{... "np_w":null,...,"np_target_candidate":null,...,"note":"... rolling NP Infinity W used directly as np_target ..."}`. JSON.stringify turns Infinity/NaN into null, so the plan.json self-contradicts (null fields vs an 'Infinity W' note) and downstream JSON consumers read a null anchor as if valid.
recommendation: Sanitize/validate FitPassMetrics before serialization (reject or fall back when np_w/mean_power_w/np_target_candidate are non-finite), so plan.json never contains null anchor numerics with a contradictory note.

title: readFitPowerBytes ignores decoder.read().errors — corrupt FIT silently treated as valid/empty ride
evidence: `const { messages } = decoder.read();` discards the `errors` array and `records ?? []`. Reproduced against real SDK-built files written to /tmp: bad-CRC and single-bit-flip files decode with errors=1 yet readFitPowerBytes returns the full [200,210,220,230,240] (CRC/integrity failure ignored); a valid-header+garbage-body file (errors=1, 'byte 13') returns []; a truncated file (errors=1, 'end of stream') still returns 5 records. Via the web path (pipeline.ts:184 `fitBytes ? readFitPowerBytes(fitBytes) : null`) a corrupt upload yields powerStream=[] (truthy bytes, not null), so determineAnchorFromPower runs analyzePass([]) and produces a misleading 'Short test ride (0.00h)' note + 163 W fallback as if the FIT were a legitimate short ride.
recommendation: Inspect `errors` (and/or decoder.checkIntegrity()) from decoder.read(); throw or surface a descriptive error on integrity failure instead of silently returning partial/empty power. Distinguish 'no FIT' (null) from 'corrupt FIT' so the pipeline does not present garbage as a valid analysis.

title: Out-of-range power wraps via uint16 storage and feeds the model unbounded (no plausibility bound)
evidence: The SDK encoder stores record power as uint16, so through a genuine FIT: power=-50 -> recovered 65486; -10 -> 65526; 70000 -> 4464 (overflow wrap); 250.7 -> 250 (truncation); 65535 and NaN are dropped as the 0xffff invalid sentinel. Reproduced a real long_neg.fit (7201 records of power=-50): readFitPowerBytes recovers 65486 for every sample and determineAnchorFromPower returns classification=long_representative, np_target_candidate=65486 W (ftp=272). Nothing clamps power to a physiological range, so a corrupt/garbage FIT yields a 65 kW anchor.
recommendation: Clamp/validate recovered watts to a sane physiological range (e.g. 0..2000 W, drop or reject outliers) before NP computation; treat the uint16 invalid sentinel explicitly. Optionally bound np_target_candidate by ftp on the long-ride path.

title: normalizedPower turns negative power into positive NP (sign lost via ^4)
evidence: `meanFourthPow = mean(rolling^4); return meanFourthPow ** 0.25`. Reproduced: normalizedPower([-100,-100,-100]) -> 100 (negative drained power reported as 100 W effort); normalizedPower(Array(40).fill(1e200)) -> Infinity (4th-power overflow). Feeds analyzePass np_w, e.g. analyzePass(Array(7201).fill(-300)) -> np_target_candidate 300.
recommendation: Reject or clamp negative samples before NP (physical power at the pedals is >=0); guard against ^4 overflow when sample magnitudes are implausibly large.

title: riderNpAtSpeed is non-monotone on descents/strong tailwind (4th-power loses braking sign); solver picks wrong low-speed branch and crawls downhill
evidence: On a -6% descent pullPower goes NEGATIVE (freewheel/brake), but riderNpAtSpeed raises it to the 4th power so |neg| reads as large effort. Measured riderNpAtSpeed(v) on grade=-0.06: rises to ~414W at v=11.5, dips to a local min ~176W at v=18.5, then rises again — clearly non-monotone. solveSpeedForRiderNp (comment: 'monotone increasing in v') bisects and lands on the WRONG low-speed root: solveSpeedForRiderNp(200,grade=-0.06)=3.86 m/s (13.9 km/h) while a valid high-speed root exists at ~19.55 m/s (70.4 km/h). Crossover is ~-4.3%/-4.5% grade.
recommendation: In solveSpeedForRiderNp/solveSpeedForPower, search for the FASTEST root consistent with the target (scan from hi end, or detect the negative-pedal-power region and root-find only on the monotone high-speed branch). Equivalently, when pedal/pull power would be <=0 at the desired speed the rider is freewheeling: pick the speed where required power crosses the target from above. Do NOT take |P| inside NP for descent segments.

title: Steeper descent yields SLOWER plan speed than flat at the same effort (wrong sign of monotonicity in grade)
evidence: runInnerSolve at npTarget=200, single 1km segment: flat(0%)=37.1 km/h/97s; -6%=13.9 km/h/259s (cap=none); -8%=10.0 km/h/360s. A descent is slower than flat, and a steeper descent is slower than a shallower one — physically backwards. With a tailwind it is worse: -6% grade + 18 m/s tailwind collapses to 7.5 km/h (cap=none). The 50 km/h spinout cap in runInnerSolve never engages because the wrong branch is far below it.
recommendation: Same fix as the riderNpAtSpeed branch bug. Add a regression guard asserting plan speed is monotone non-decreasing as grade decreases (and as tailwind increases) at fixed npTarget.

title: Production Vatternrundan route: 118 microsegments (3.8 km) crawl the buggy descent branch (median 14.9 km/h, min 4.3 km/h)
evidence: ingestGpxString of data/vatternrundan-315km.gpx yields 4764 microsegments, grade range -0.1800..0.1597 (max_grade clip = 0.18). 118 effort segments (2.5%, 3.8 km) are steeper than -4.3% and hit the buggy branch. Speeds on those descents: min 4.3, median 14.9, max 50.0 km/h. Example grade=-0.054 -> solver 16.1 km/h vs correct high-speed root ~67.2 km/h. So the bug fires on the shipped default route, not just synthetic inputs.
recommendation: Fix the descent root-selection (findings above); the wrong descent times inflate required NP elsewhere in the bisection, biasing the whole plan. Re-baseline the Vatternrundan validation numbers after the fix.

title: n_riders=0 and pull_seconds=0 produce NaN rider NP (npMomentsFor divides by cycle length n=0)
evidence: riderNpAtSpeed(8,0,0,0,1.2,cfg{n_riders:0}) = NaN and riderNpAtSpeed(...,{pull_seconds:0}) = NaN. occupancyArray builds an array of length n = nRiders*pullSeconds = 0, npMomentsFor divides each cN by n=0 -> NaN, propagated into npFromMoments. (In full runInnerSolve these are partly masked because solo/path differences, but the chaingang primitive returns NaN directly.) applyDefaults does not validate n_riders>0 or pull_seconds>0.
recommendation: Validate n_riders>=1 and pull_seconds>=1 in applyDefaults (throw a descriptive error), or guard npMomentsFor against n===0.

title: Negative stop minutes flow through unchecked: negative total_time_s/stop_time_s and broken ETA monotonicity
evidence: solveForTargetTime with stops=[{control:'X',km:10,minutes:-600}] gives total_time_s=-27716.8 and stop_time_s=-36000, and segment eta_s is no longer monotonically increasing (a later segment's ETA jumps backward). addS = stop.minutes*60 is added with no >=0 guard.
recommendation: Clamp stop.minutes to >=0 (or validate in applyDefaults). The solver and downstream renderers assume non-decreasing ETAs.

title: FTP<=0 inverts the outer-solver bracket (loNp=60 > hiNp=ftp) and zeroes the intensity factor without flagging unreachable
evidence: With ftp=0: pull_cap_hard=0, solveForTargetTime returns np=60, total=10180, reachable=true (the [60,0] bracket is inverted; bisection still 'works' by luck because total<=target). intensity_factor = ftp>0 ? np/ftp : 0, so a redline plan reports IF=0 and the sustain warning is silently suppressed. Negative ftp (-272) gives pull caps -354/-250, np=60, IF=0, reachable=true — no error.
recommendation: Validate ftp>0 in applyDefaults (throw), or guard the outer solver: if hiNp<=loNp, return a clearly-flagged unreachable/degenerate result rather than a misleadingly 'reachable' plan with IF=0.

title: Shape-only date regex forwards semantically-invalid dates (month 13, day 45, 0000-00-00, Feb 31) straight into upstream Open-Meteo URLs
evidence: ISO_DATE = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ only checks shape. Fuzz (tsx, fetch stubbed to capture forwarded URLs) shows pts='58.5,14.6' with date='2026-13-01' is ACCEPTED (status 200, parsedDate '2026-13-01') and forwarded verbatim: 'https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?...&start_date=2026-13-01&end_date=2026-13-01&timezone=UTC'. Same for '2026-01-45', '0000-00-00', '9999-99-99', '2026-02-31', '2026-00-10', '2026-01-00', '2026-12-99' (all accepted:true). The handler comment claims 'always 400 on bad query' but these never 400; they reach gatherWindSamples and hit the upstream APIs.
recommendation: After the regex passes, validate the date is real: e.g. const d=new Date(date+'T00:00:00Z'); reject when Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) || d.toISOString().slice(0,10)!==date. Optionally bound the range (e.g. within +/- a forecast window) so a caller cannot drive cache-busting upstream fetches with arbitrary far-future/past dates. Failing validation should return the existing 400 path.

title: Number() coercion accepts hex/octal/binary literals as coordinates, silently mutating input (0x1 -> lat 1, 0o10 -> 8, 0b101 -> 5)
evidence: parseWeatherQuery uses lat=Number(latS),lon=Number(lonS) then only checks Number.isFinite + range. Fuzz: pts='0x1,14.6' -> accepted:true points:[{lat:1,lon:14.6}]; '0o10,14.6' -> lat:8; '0b101,14.6' -> lat:5. These pass the in-range guard and are forwarded as real coordinates ('...latitude=1&longitude=14.6...'). A malformed/garbage token that the author plainly never intended as a number is silently reinterpreted instead of rejected.
recommendation: Validate the numeric token's textual form before Number(), e.g. require /^[+-]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(e[+-]?\d+)?$/i on the trimmed half (rejecting 0x/0o/0b prefixes), or parse with a strict float parser. Keep the existing isFinite+range checks as a second layer.

title: Surrounding whitespace/tabs/newlines in coordinate tokens are silently accepted (Number trims)
evidence: Fuzz: pts='  58.5 , 14.6 ' -> accepted:true points:[{lat:58.5,lon:14.6}]; '58.5,14.6\t' and '\n58.5,14.6' also accepted. Number('  58.5  ') trims whitespace, so tokens with embedded surrounding whitespace pass. The non-empty guard (!latS) only catches the empty string, not whitespace-only-adjacent values. Inconsistent with the otherwise-strict intent.
recommendation: Trim and reject tokens containing internal whitespace, or apply the strict numeric-format regex from the previous finding (which forbids leading/trailing whitespace). Low risk but worth tightening alongside the hex fix.

title: parseWeatherQuery has no try/catch; a non-string element inside a pts array throws 'pts.split is not a function' instead of returning 400
evidence: first() unwraps an array to v[0] but does not coerce to string. Fuzz with q={date:'2026-06-13', pts:[{toString(){...}}]} produced an unhandled throw: 'pts.split is not a function or its return value is not iterable' (no 400, exception escapes handleWeather, which has no surrounding try/catch). In practice Vercel's req.query yields string|string[] so this exact shape is unlikely, hence low severity, but the handler relies on that assumption with no defensive guard. The weather.ts adapter (api/weather.ts:5) does not wrap handleWeather either, so a throw becomes a 500.
recommendation: In first(), coerce the unwrapped value to a string only when typeof === 'string' (else treat as undefined), or guard typeof pts === 'string' before pts.split. Alternatively wrap the handleWeather body / the weather.ts call site in try/catch returning a 400/500 JSON body so the endpoint can never surface an unstructured runtime error.

title: Confirmed safe: injection chars, out-of-range coords, over-cap, huge pts, unicode, empty all 400 with zero upstream fetches
evidence: Fuzz (tsx, real handler, fetch stubbed): pts='58.5,14.6&evil=1', '../../etc/passwd', '58.5,14.6\r\nHost: evil' all -> status 400, nForwarded 0. Out-of-range '100,14.6'/'58.5,200' -> 400. 'NaN,14.6','Infinity,14.6','1e308,14.6' -> 400. 65 points and 100000 points -> 400 (100k rejected in 37ms before any fetch). Unicode digits '٥٨,١٤' and fullwidth '５８.５,...' -> 400. The strict ISO date charset (\d and -) means the date cannot carry URL-injection payloads. No crash on any realistic input.
recommendation: No action; documents the boundaries the validator does enforce so the date/hex gaps above are seen in context.

title: strict: true enabled globally via tsconfig.base.json (inherited by all packages)
evidence: "strict": true,  -- set once in the base config; root, packages/core, packages/cli, apps/web, and api all extend it. This transitively enables noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, strictFunctionTypes, etc.
recommendation: Good baseline. strict (hence noImplicitAny) is ON everywhere. No package overrides strict to false.

title: noUncheckedIndexedAccess is OFF (never set in any tsconfig)
evidence: grep across tsconfig.base.json + all 5 package tsconfigs finds no occurrence of noUncheckedIndexedAccess. The base compilerOptions block (target, module, strict, esModuleInterop, resolveJsonModule, skipLibCheck, lib, types, paths) does not include it.
recommendation: Array/record index access (e.g. weather parsers iterating json arrays in packages/core/src/weather/*.ts, gpx point arrays) is typed as non-undefined even when out of bounds. Consider enabling noUncheckedIndexedAccess given the heavy raw-JSON/array parsing of external weather APIs and GPX/FIT data.

title: exactOptionalPropertyTypes is OFF (never set)
evidence: No occurrence of exactOptionalPropertyTypes in tsconfig.base.json or any package tsconfig. Not implied by strict.
recommendation: Optional. Enabling it would tighten the many optional fields in core types (e.g. WindSample, FitMesg [field]?: FitFieldValue|undefined in output/fitWorkout.ts). Low priority.

title: Root tsconfig typecheck passes clean (core + cli + tests together: 0 errors)
evidence: Project's own `typecheck` script is `tsc --noEmit && tsc --noEmit -p api/tsconfig.json && npm run typecheck -w apps/web`. Running `tsc --noEmit` from repo root (uses tsconfig.json -> tsconfig.base.json which `include`s packages/*/src and packages/*/tests) => exit 0, 0 errors. packages/core standalone => exit 0. apps/web standalone => exit 0.
recommendation: The core/web/root typecheck is healthy. TS compiler version is typescript@6.0.3 (devDependencies "^6.0.3"); this is a notably new major, verify CI uses the same to avoid drift.

title: API typecheck FAILS: @vercel/node declared but not installed (TS2307)
evidence: `import type { VercelRequest, VercelResponse } from '@vercel/node';` -> error TS2307: Cannot find module '@vercel/node'. Reproduces both as `tsc --noEmit` in api/ and via the project command `tsc --noEmit -p api/tsconfig.json` (exit 2). Root package.json declares "@vercel/node": "^5.8.12" in devDependencies, but `node_modules/@vercel/node` and `node_modules/.pnpm/@vercel+node@*` do NOT exist. There is no api/package.json.
recommendation: Run a full install. Git status shows untracked pnpm-lock.yaml + pnpm-workspace.yaml (a pnpm migration in progress) while scripts still invoke `npm` and `npm run -w`; the dependency tree is incomplete. The api typecheck (and Vercel build) will fail until @vercel/node is actually installed.

title: CLI standalone typecheck reports 31 errors, but they are rootDir/config artifacts, not real type bugs
evidence: Running tsc in packages/cli => exit 2, 31 errors: 25x TS6059 ('File .../packages/core/src/*.ts is not under rootDir packages/cli') because cli/tsconfig sets rootDir:'.' yet imports @stp/core source via paths mapping into the sibling package, plus 6x TS2305 ('Module @garmin/fitsdk has no exported member Decoder/Stream' in tests/fitWorkout.test.ts). The same files compile cleanly under the root tsconfig (0 errors). The project has no per-package cli typecheck wired into the root `typecheck` script.
recommendation: Not a real defect in CLI source; it is how the task ran tsc per-package. The TS2305 in fitWorkout.test.ts indicates the ambient @garmin/fitsdk declaration (packages/core/src/garmin-fitsdk.d.ts) is not on the include path for cli tests; if a standalone cli typecheck is ever desired, add the .d.ts to cli's include and use project references / composite instead of rootDir.

title: Cast/any inventory: 77 ' as ', 8 ': any', 2 'as any', 1 'as unknown', 1 'as Array'; zero @ts-ignore/@ts-expect-error
evidence: Across 54 .ts/.tsx files in packages/core/src, packages/cli/src, apps/web/src, api: ' as ' x77 (most are `as const`, type imports, or harmless DOM/literal casts), ': any' x8, 'as any' x2, 'as unknown' x1, 'as Array' x1. No @ts-ignore (0) and no @ts-expect-error (0) anywhere.
recommendation: Suppression comments are absent (good). The risk concentrates in untyped external-JSON parsing (weather) and the cross-SDK FIT casts below.

title: Web weather response is cast to EnsembleField with no runtime validation
evidence: `return (await res.json()) as EnsembleField;` -- the /api/weather response body is blindly asserted to EnsembleField. Only res.ok is checked (line 16); the JSON shape is never validated, so a malformed/changed API payload propagates as a wrongly-typed object into the solver.
recommendation: Validate the parsed JSON (zod or a hand-written guard) before returning, or at least narrow key fields. This is the highest-value cast to harden because it crosses the network trust boundary.

title: Core weather parsers accept raw external JSON as 'any' (openMeteo, smhi, metNorway)
evidence: parseOpenMeteo(json: any, ...) line 72 and 129; smhi.ts parseSmhi(json: any) line 32 with `const timeSeries: any[] = json?.timeSeries ?? []` (33), `const params: any[]` (37), `params.find((x: any) => ...)` (40); metNorway.ts parseMetNorway(json: any) line 50 + `const timeseries: any[]` line 51. 6 of the 8 ': any' usages are here. Field access like `h.windspeed_10m ?? []` (openMeteo.ts:80) is unchecked.
recommendation: These are the source-of-truth parsers for three upstream weather APIs. Replace `any` with `unknown` + explicit narrowing or a schema. With noUncheckedIndexedAccess off and any inputs, a shape change silently yields NaN/empty samples rather than a type error.

title: FIT workout encoder uses double cast through unknown (as unknown as ...)
evidence: `encoder.writeMesg(mesg as unknown as Parameters<Encoder['writeMesg']>[0]);` -- the only 'as unknown' in the codebase. Comment (48-50) explains the Garmin SDK's writeMesg param type is narrower than the runtime accepts. The ambient decl (garmin-fitsdk.d.ts) types writeMesg(mesg: Record<string,unknown>).
recommendation: Acceptable and documented; it bridges a known SDK typing gap. Low risk since FitMesg is a locally controlled shape. Leave as-is or align the ambient writeMesg signature with FitMesg.

title: FIT ingest (fit.ts) is comparatively well-typed; recordMesgs leaks 'any[]' via ambient decl
evidence: fit.ts itself contains NO ' as ' casts and NO ': any' (the two grep hits at lines 32,57 are prose in comments). It uses `const records: Array<{ power?: unknown }> = messages.recordMesgs ?? []` (18). However `messages` is typed `Record<string, any[]>` in garmin-fitsdk.d.ts (decoder.read returns `{ messages: Record<string, any[]> ... }`), so recordMesgs is an `any[]` whose elements are then re-typed to `{power?: unknown}`.
recommendation: fit.ts handles untyped SDK output safely by re-annotating to unknown and filtering. The residual looseness is in the ambient .d.ts (Record<string, any[]>); tightening recordMesgs to a typed message shape would remove the last any path, but current handling is defensive. Contrary to the task's prior, fit.ts is not a high-risk cast site.

title: GPX parser casts fast-xml-parser output to Record/Array of unknown
evidence: `const trksegObj = trkseg as Record<string, unknown>;` (34) and `const points = trkpts as Array<Record<string, unknown>>;` (41) -- the sole 'as Array'. Then fields are coerced via Number(pt['@_lat']) etc (44-46), so a missing/garbage field yields NaN rather than a thrown error.
recommendation: Casts to unknown-keyed records are reasonable for XML; the real gap is no validation that lat/lon are finite numbers. Consider guarding Number(...) results (Number.isFinite) before building points.

title: Two 'as any' casts are confined to API tests (not production code)
evidence: `expect((res.body as any).cells.length)...` (58) and `(res.body as any).sources` (59). Both 'as any' occurrences in the repo are in test assertions, none in shipped source.
recommendation: Acceptable in tests. No action needed.

title: Suite status: 308 tests, 307 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip across 34 test files
