recommendation: No action: business logic in handler.ts is tested; weather.ts is a 4-line platform shim.

title: All packages/core/src modules are covered (directly or via @stp/core export) — no zero-test core module
evidence: ingest/fit.ts (analyzePass/readFitPowerBytes/determineAnchorFromPower), output/fitWorkout.ts (buildSteps/encodeWorkout), output/planJson.ts (buildPlanJson), output/course.ts (buildCourseGpx) are exercised via cli/tests/{fit,fitWorkout,planJson,gpx}.test.ts and core/tests; ciq/template.ts is consumed by the tested ciq/generate.ts (PLAN_DELTA_TEMPLATE). config.ts/types.ts used throughout. Only types/decl files (types.ts, garmin-fitsdk.d.ts) lack assertions, as expected.
recommendation: Core is the best-covered area. Note coverage is by file presence, not line/branch — install a coverage provider to confirm depth within these modules (e.g. error/edge branches in physics, segmentation).

title: @vercel/node toolchain pulls 9 known vulnerabilities (6 high, 3 moderate) into the dependency tree
evidence: Root devDep "@vercel/node": "^5.8.12". npm audit metadata: {moderate:3, high:6, critical:0, total:9}. Vulnerable transitives via @vercel/node: path-to-regexp (GHSA-9wv6-86v2-598j high ReDoS), minimatch (GHSA-7r86-cg39-jmmj / GHSA-23c5-xmqv-rm74 high ReDoS), undici (GHSA-c76h-2ccp-4975 + GHSA-g9mf-h72j-4rw9), smol-toml (GHSA-v3rj-xjv7-4jmq moderate DoS), ajv (GHSA-2g4f-4pwh-qvx6 moderate ReDoS). All flow through @vercel/build-utils / @vercel/python-analysis / @vercel/static-config.
recommendation: Dev/build-time only (used for VercelRequest/VercelResponse types in api/weather.ts and typecheck; not bundled at runtime per api/handler.ts comment). npm fixAvailable points to @vercel/node@4.0.0 (a DOWNGRADE from ^5.8.12, an npm advisory metadata quirk). Run npm audit fix or upgrade to a 5.x patch that bumps transitives; or drop @vercel/node entirely and hand-roll the two TS types since that is its only use.

title: path-to-regexp ReDoS (high) reachable only via @vercel/node dev toolchain
evidence: audit: path-to-regexp range "4.0.0 - 6.2.2", GHSA-9wv6-86v2-598j CVSS 7.5 'outputs backtracking regular expressions'. effects: @vercel/node.
recommendation: Resolved by updating the @vercel/node toolchain. Not on the runtime request path; the weather endpoint validates input in parseWeatherQuery and does not use path-to-regexp.

title: undici insufficient-randomness + unbounded-decompression DoS (moderate) in dev tree
evidence: audit: undici GHSA-c76h-2ccp-4975 (CVSS 6.8) and GHSA-g9mf-h72j-4rw9 (CVSS 5.9 unbounded decompression chain DoS), range <6.23.0 / <5.28.5. Pulled by @vercel/node.
recommendation: Bump via @vercel/node update. Runtime weather fetches use Node 22 global fetch, not this undici copy, so production impact is minimal.

title: No engines field and no .nvmrc - Node version unpinned across all 4 package.json files
evidence: grep '"engines"' across all package.json: NONE FOUND. .nvmrc absent. Local Node v22.22.2 but nothing enforces it; deps assume modern Node (React 19, Vite 6, @vercel/node 5, global fetch in api/handler.ts).
recommendation: Add "engines":{"node":">=20"} (or >=22) to root package.json and commit .nvmrc/.node-version. api/handler.ts relies on built-in global fetch and the weather path deliberately avoids bundling undici; an older Node without global fetch would break at runtime. Vercel also reads this for the deploy runtime.

title: Competing lockfiles on disk but pnpm artifacts correctly gitignored and untracked - package-lock.json is canonical
evidence: git ls-files shows only package-lock.json tracked (pnpm-lock.yaml/pnpm-workspace.yaml NOT tracked). .gitignore comment: 'this repo uses npm (package-lock.json); ignore stray pnpm lockfiles'. Both pnpm files exist as untracked (?? in git status, pnpm-lock.yaml 32.8K).
recommendation: No correctness action; npm lockfile is single source of truth and vercel.json uses installCommand 'npm install'. Optional: delete the stray pnpm-lock.yaml/pnpm-workspace.yaml from the working tree to avoid misleading a contributor or pnpm-autodetecting CI.

title: Audit/lockfile tree out of sync with installed node_modules (partial install)
evidence: node_modules/@vercel/node, node_modules/undici, node_modules/path-to-regexp NOT present on disk (ls -> NOT INSTALLED), yet npm audit reports them - audit reads package-lock.json, not the installed tree.
recommendation: Run npm ci to reconcile node_modules with package-lock.json. Does not change the vulnerability facts (they live in the committed lockfile) but local typecheck of the api dir may fail without @vercel/node installed.

title: Web devDeps behind by full majors: vite 6->8, jsdom 25->29, @vitejs/plugin-react 4->6
evidence: npm outdated: vite 6.4.3 -> latest 8.0.16; jsdom 25.0.1 -> 29.1.1; @vitejs/plugin-react 4.7.0 -> 6.0.2. Declared ^6 / ^25 / ^4.
recommendation: Plan major upgrades for the web dev toolchain (Vite is two majors behind). Dev-only, low urgency, but Vite 6 will lose security support. Also note typescript ^6.0.3 and @types/node ^25.9.1 are very new majors - verify they resolve to real published versions in CI.

title: No secrets committed - developer_key.der and .env correctly gitignored and untracked
evidence: git ls-files grep for developer_key/.der/.env/.pem/secret/key: none tracked. ciq/developer_key.der exists on disk (perms -rw------- 2374 bytes) but gitignored/untracked. No .env files present. git grep for api_key/secret/token/bearer literals and AKIA/AIza/sk-/ghp_ patterns in tracked source: zero matches. config.json holds only race params (ftp, dates), no credentials.
recommendation: No action. Secret hygiene is correct: Garmin signing key (ciq/developer_key.der), build artifacts (ciq/bin/, *.prg), .env, and generated ciq/source/*.mc are all ignored. Keep the 0600 permission on developer_key.der.

title: Runtime production deps are minimal and low-risk (@garmin/fitsdk, fast-xml-parser, react)
evidence: audit metadata: prod dependencies = 17 (dev=395). @stp/core deps: @garmin/fitsdk ^21.205.0 (official Garmin SDK), fast-xml-parser ^5.8.0 (actively maintained, no advisory in this audit). @stp/web runtime deps: react/react-dom ^19. No abandoned or flagged-vulnerable runtime package found.
recommendation: No action. The runtime/production surface is clean - all 9 vulnerabilities are confined to the dev/build toolchain. fast-xml-parser has had past ReDoS advisories so keep it patched (current ^5.8.0 is clear here).

title: segmentation.ts is a god file dominated by one 243-line god function with very high cyclomatic complexity
evidence: export function segment(plan, cfg, controls, opts) {...} spans lines 277-520 (243 LOC of a 520 LOC file). The file has 85 branch tokens (if/for/while/case/&&/||), by far the most in the codebase. segment() alone contains 4 sequential `while (changed) { for (...) { ... break; } }` merge passes (minSegmentKm merge L417-449, grade merge L462-483, maxSegments merge L490-517) plus boundary building (L290-332) and group assembly (L345-393).
recommendation: Split segment() into named helpers: buildBoundaries(), buildGroups(), and a generic mergeWhile(predicate, pick) that the three near-identical O(n^2) while/for/break merge passes can share. Each merge pass currently re-implements the same restart-scan pattern.

title: mergeDisplaySegs reconstructs numeric state from already-rendered fields (lossy, fragile)
evidence: The function comments admit the design smell: "recompute from the already-labeled strings is not ideal, but we need numeric values" (L188-192), and band_pct is reverse-engineered: "band_pct ~ (high - low) / (2 * mid)" with `const bandRatio = aPullMid > 0 ? (a.pull_w_high - a.pull_w_low) / (2 * aPullMid) : 0;` (L211). Wind label is picked by larger-distance half rather than recomputed (L216).
recommendation: Carry the numeric mean headwind / pull-mean on the Group/DisplaySegment (or merge at the Group level before aggregation) so merges do not have to invert rounded display values. This removes the band-ratio reconstruction and the distance-dominant heuristics.

title: UploadForm.tsx is the largest web file (364 LOC) mixing persistence, file IO, and a large form
evidence: Single component UploadForm spans L86-364 (~278 LOC) holding 11 useState hooks (L91-107), localStorage persistence (loadFromStorage/saveToStorage/persist), two async file-read handlers, three stop-list mutators, and the full JSX. Every input duplicates an inline `onChange={(e) => { setX(v); persist({ x: v }); }}` pattern.
recommendation: Extract a usePersistedForm() hook for the state+localStorage glue and a <StopsEditor> subcomponent for the stops table; the repeated set+persist inline handlers can be replaced by a single typed field updater.

title: runInnerSolve carries the inner solver's full per-segment branching in one ~157-line function
evidence: runInnerSolve spans L96-253 (~157 LOC). The effort branch nests cap selection (hard L154, soft else-if L158-166 with a 3-condition &&), then a separate none/else recompute branch (L170-181), then a stops post-pass with a nested `for (let j = idx; ...) segments[j].eta_s += addS;` (L224-226). Mixed concerns: neutral handling, effort+caps, and stop-delay rewriting.
recommendation: Extract solveEffortSegment(micro, npTarget, ...) returning a SegmentPlan, and applyStops(segments, cfg) for the delay pass. The outer loop then reads as march-then-apply-stops.

title: runPlan orchestration function (~124 LOC) interleaves IO, weather fallback logic, and artifact writing
evidence: runPlan spans L88-212 (~124 LOC) and is the bulk of cli.ts's 32 branch tokens: config+mkdir, GPX existence check, anchor, a multi-branch weather cache->fetch->ensemble->calm fallback (L107-139), scenario solve, segmentation, unreachable-target markdown patching (L151-157), five artifact writes, and a try/catch CIQ compile (L178-191).
recommendation: Extract resolveWeatherField(cfg, opts) (returning {field, useCalm, reducedEnsemble, notes, sources}) and writeArtifacts(...). runPlan then reads as a short pipeline.

title: chaingang.ts: nested O(window*n) loops in circularRollingMean30 / occupancyArray with modulo-wrap indexing
evidence: circularRollingMean30 has a double loop with `const idx = ((i - j) % n + n) % n;` (L107) and occupancyArray repeats the identical 30-window modulo-wrap pattern (L182-195). 25 branch tokens in the file; the two functions duplicate the same windowing logic, which the closed-form npFromMoments was built to replace.
recommendation: These are reference/precompute paths and acceptable, but the duplicated circular-window indexing (L98-114 vs L182-195) could share one helper. Low priority since occupancyArray output is cached.

title: makeWeatherFn returns a closure doing a full linear cell scan per query (per-segment, per-scenario)
evidence: The returned WeatherFn loops over all cells computing a haversine + score on every call: `for (const cell of cells) { const distM = haversine(...); ... if (score < bestScore) ... }` (L241-255). This runs once per microsegment per scenario inside the bisection solver (45 iterations x 3 scenarios x N segments), making nearest-cell lookup an O(cells) hot path.
recommendation: If cell counts grow, index cells by (roundedLat, roundedLon, hour) into a Map for O(1) candidate lookup instead of scanning all cells every query. Currently cell counts are small (route-sampled), so impact is bounded.

title: riderNpSquareWaveReference is exported but only referenced by tests (reference-only export)
evidence: grep shows riderNpSquareWaveReference is used only in packages/core/tests/chaingang.test.ts (L8,151) and named in a doc comment; no production caller. It is the O(n) oracle the O(1) npFromMoments is validated against (comment L131-134, L260-264).
recommendation: Intentional and correct as a test oracle. No change needed; optionally annotate as @internal/test-only to signal it is not part of the consumed API surface.

title: fetchSmhi and fetchMetNorway are re-exported from @stp/core index but consumed only internally
evidence: index.ts L63 re-exports `gatherWindSamples, fetchSmhi, fetchMetNorway, mapLimit`. grep shows fetchSmhi/fetchMetNorway have no external consumers, only internal use inside fetchAll.ts (L83-84). gatherWindSamples and mapLimit do have external/test consumers.
recommendation: Narrow the public surface: drop fetchSmhi/fetchMetNorway from the index re-export (keep them module-local) unless they are intended as a supported API. Low impact, surface-area hygiene only.

title: Files over 250 LOC (size inventory)
evidence: Files exceeding 250 LOC under the scanned roots: segmentation.ts 520, apps/web/src/components/UploadForm.tsx 364, output/tempokort.ts 360, planner.ts 358, chaingang.ts 313, cli/src/cli.ts 292, weather/ensemble.ts 278. tempokort.ts (360) is large mostly due to two big embedded CSS string constants (HTML_STYLE L171-214, STYRKORT_STYLE L216-256) and is low-complexity (only 8 branch tokens).
recommendation: Prioritize refactoring by complexity, not raw LOC: segmentation.ts first, then planner.ts/cli.ts. tempokort.ts is long but trivial (string templates) and not worth splitting beyond optionally moving the two CSS constants to a styles module.

title: Entire Connect IQ data field (NextControlPace.mc) has zero findings despite being an untrusted-input boundary
evidence: 349-line Monkey C file parses course-point names live (parsePlannedSec, isRelativeName) and computes ETA/delta; the file is uncommitted-modified (git status shows 'M ciq/source/NextControlPace.mc') yet no prior finding references any ciq/ path.
recommendation: Audit NextControlPace.mc as a first-class boundary: it parses attacker/author-controlled course-point name strings off the FIT course and renders on-watch. Review parsePlannedSec, isRelativeName, fmtClock, and the segment-change heuristics for robustness.

title: CIQ parsePlannedSec silently drops plan delta for elapsed labels >= 24h or any HH:MM the watch font cannot represent
evidence: parsePlannedSec returns a time only `if (hh < 24 && mm < 60)`, but relative-mode labels come from secondsToElapsed which formats H:MM with NO 24h cap (util/time.ts:43-48, `const hh = Math.floor(total / 3600)`). A plan over 24h (e.g. '+25:30') is silently rejected and the rider sees no plan delta for that control.
recommendation: Either cap/validate elapsed labels in secondsToElapsed, or relax the hh<24 guard in relative mode (elapsed hours can legitimately exceed 24). The field is documented as 'generic, install-once' so it should not assume a sub-24h plan.

title: CIQ fmtClock assumes ETA seconds < 86400; relative-mode delta math can also wrap incorrectly
evidence: etaClock is computed as `(nowSec + etaSec.toNumber()) % 86400` (line 186) so fmtClock's `s/3600` is bounded, but in absolute mode the delta `d = etaClock - planned` is wrap-corrected by +/-43200 while relative mode `d = (elapsedSec + etaSec) - planned` has no bound and assumes planned is sub-day elapsed; large elapsed plans were never reasoned about.
recommendation: Add a test/spec for relative-mode delta when elapsed exceeds 12h/24h, and confirm fmtClock/fmtDelta behave for multi-hour deltas.

title: course.ts nearestMicroIndex / nearestEtaS crash on empty microsegments (unguarded micros[0])
evidence: nearestMicroIndex does `let bestDiff = Math.abs(micros[0].cum_distance_m - targetM)` with no length check; buildCourseGpx calls it per control. An empty/degenerate route (which the GPX findings show is reachable) throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined'. nearestEtaS guards segs.length but nearestMicroIndex does not guard micros.
recommendation: Guard micros.length===0 in nearestMicroIndex (and the microsegments[] reads in buildCourseGpx) the same way nearestEtaS guards plan.segments, returning a validated error instead of a raw TypeError.

title: fitCourse.ts crashes on empty/single microsegment route (unguarded first/last access)
evidence: `const last = microsegments[microsegments.length - 1]` and `const first = microsegments[0]` are read with no length guard before `last.cum_distance_m` and `toSemicircles(first.lat)`. An empty route (reachable per the GPX edge-case findings) throws an opaque TypeError inside the FIT course writer with no UI/CLI feedback.
recommendation: Validate microsegments.length>=1 (ideally >=2 for a navigable course) at the top of buildCourseFit and throw a descriptive error.

title: tempokort Markdown table injection: unescaped pipe in town/note breaks GFM pipe-table structure
evidence: renderMarkdown emits `| ${cells.join(' | ')} |` where cells include seg.town and seg.note verbatim; escHtml (used only in the HTML path) escapes &<>" but never the pipe '|'. A control/town name or note containing '|' corrupts the GFM table column alignment. The HTML renderer escapes HTML metacharacters but also does not escape '|', and neither path escapes Markdown control chars.
recommendation: Escape '|' (and ideally newlines) for the Markdown table cells, and add a test with a town/note containing a pipe to lock the behavior.

title: web hours.ts raceHours/centroidOf unvalidated: NaN time tokens and a local-vs-UTC hour mismatch in the weather window
evidence: raceHours does `startTime.split(':').map(Number)` and `targetHm.split(':').map(Number)` with no validation; a malformed h:mm yields NaN hour bounds. The hours it returns are local wall-clock (0..23) but they are matched in summarizeHourly/buildManualField against weather cells keyed `${raceDate}T${HH}:00:00Z` (UTC), so the web weather window is built on the same UTC/local confusion flagged for ensemble.ts but in an unexamined module.
recommendation: Validate the h:mm inputs and resolve the local-vs-UTC hour binning explicitly (raceHours and buildManualField currently treat local hours as UTC). Add tests for malformed time and for a non-UTC race timezone.

title: CLI plan never applies baked per-segment exposure, so CLI and web wind models silently diverge
evidence: `grep applyExposure|exposure|bakedExposure` over packages/cli/src/cli.ts returns 0 matches, while apps/web/src/lib/pipeline.ts:176-178 calls applyExposure(micro, bakedExposure) for the default route. The CLI therefore uses only the coarse cfg.exposure_terrain ('mixed') while the web uses real OSM land cover, producing different effective wind and thus different plans for the same route.
recommendation: Apply data/vatternrundan-exposure.json in the CLI default-route path (or document the divergence). This is a distinct mechanism from the README 'identical results' finding, which only cited differing control sets.

title: applyExposure midpoint binning leaves half-open-interval gaps and never asserts run coverage
evidence: applyExposure matches each microsegment by `midKm >= r.from_km && midKm < r.to_km` (half-open). Any midpoint falling exactly on a boundary gap, or beyond the last run's to_km, silently keeps no exposure_class and falls back to coarse terrain; exposureCoveragePct exists but is never asserted against a threshold in core. No prior finding examines exposure.ts.
recommendation: Consider closing the last interval or snapping boundary midpoints, and surface low exposure coverage (e.g. warn when exposureCoveragePct < some threshold) rather than silently degrading to terrain.

title: doFetch builds the weather config without exposure/height/default-route flags, diverging from the solve config
evidence: doFetch calls applyDefaults({...}) WITHOUT exposure_terrain, apply_wind_height_correction, or is_default_route, then ingestGpxString + sampleCellPoints + centroidOf off that config. The pipeline (handleRun -> runPipeline) builds a different cfg that DOES apply exposure and height correction, so the sampled cell points / centroid used for the fetch are computed from a route ingested under different settings than the one that is solved.
recommendation: Build the fetch-time cfg from the same form flags as runPipeline (or share one config builder) so sampling and solving agree.

title: buildManualField hardcodes temp 10C / pressure 101325 Pa and treats manual hours as UTC
evidence: buildManualField stamps `temp_c: 10, pressure_pa: 101_325` for every cell and builds time_iso as `${raceDate}T${HH}:00:00Z` from local hour numbers; no finding examines hourly.ts. The fixed temp/pressure silently override real air-density inputs in manual mode and the Z suffix repeats the UTC/local mismatch.
recommendation: Let manual mode carry user temp/pressure (or document the fixed values as intentional) and align hour-to-timestamp with the rest of the pipeline.

title: controlsFromStops places 'Mål' at a fractional routeEndKm that buildCourseGpx matches only by exact cp.km, risking a wrong waypoint snap
evidence: controlsFromStops sets the finish control km = micro[last].cum_distance_m/1000 (a fractional km). buildCourseGpx (course.ts:118) matches stop minutes by `stopMinutesForKm.get(cp.km)` using exact-equality km keys and places the waypoint at nearestMicroIndex(cp.km*1000); the stop-km map uses the user's integer stop.km while controls use fractional finish km, so a stop coinciding with the finish would not match. Untested interaction between web controlsFromStops and the core course builder.
recommendation: Add a test that exercises buildCourseGpx/buildCourseFit with web-style controlsFromStops (fractional Mål km, stops near the end) to confirm waypoint placement and stop-minute annotation are correct.

title: downloadBlob and the main-thread download path have no error handling and DOM-mutate without try/finally
evidence: downloadBlob appends an anchor and calls a.click() then removeChild; if any builder upstream (encodeWorkout/buildCourseGpx/buildCourseFit) throws on the main thread there is no catch (corroborates the existing Downloads.tsx finding) and the URL.revokeObjectURL is skipped on a mid-function throw. No dedicated test exists (confirmed by the coverage-gap finding list).
recommendation: Wrap the build+download in try/catch with user feedback and revoke the object URL in a finally; add a smoke test.

title: fetchExposureForRoute stub throws by design; confirm the UI trigger is actually kept disabled
evidence: fetchExposureForRoute unconditionally throws 'Exponeringshämtning ... inte implementerad ännu (TODO task8)'. No finding references this file. If any code path can invoke it (the comment says callers must keep the trigger disabled) it surfaces as an unhandled rejection.
recommendation: Grep for callers and verify the trigger is disabled in the shipped UI; otherwise the stub becomes a user-visible crash. Low risk but unverified.

title: FIT workout encoder uses new Date() for timeCreated, breaking byte-level reproducibility (contradicts the deterministic course encoder)
evidence: encodeWorkout writes `timeCreated: new Date()` in file_id, whereas sibling buildCourseFit uses a fixed constant: `BASE_MS = Date.UTC(2026,0,1,...)` with comment 'Using a constant (never new Date()) keeps the encoded bytes deterministic for tests.' The two FIT writers disagree on the same rule.
recommendation: Replace `new Date()` in fitWorkout.ts with the same fixed BASE_MS constant (or a caller-injected clock) so workout.fit is reproducible/testable byte-for-byte like course.fit. The watch re-times the workout, so a synthetic date is harmless.

title: Watch parsePlannedSec scans the entire course-point name and will mis-parse digits inside user-supplied control town names
evidence: Course-point names are `${cp.name} ${timeLabel}` (fitCourse.ts:147). On uploaded routes cp.name is free-text cfg.stops[].control. parsePlannedSec returns the FIRST HH:MM-shaped match anywhere in the string, so any town containing 'NN:NN' or digits adjacent to the time makes the watch read the wrong planned time and show a bogus +/- delta.
recommendation: Parse the planned time only from the encoder-controlled suffix (anchor on trailing token or a sentinel separator) instead of scanning the whole free-text name; or strip/sanitize digits from control names in fitCourse.ts before appending the time label.

title: Relative-mode course-point labels use non-zero-padded hour (+H:MM) and break the watch delta for rides at/over 24h elapsed
evidence: secondsToElapsed emits `${hh}:${mm}` with hh unpadded/unbounded, while the watch only accepts hh<24 (NextControlPace.mc:104 `if (hh < 24 && mm < 60)`). A planned elapsed of 24h+ yields a label the watch silently refuses to parse, dropping the delta with no indication. Absolute mode wraps via mod 86400 but relative mode does not.
recommendation: Bound/document the supported elapsed range, or let the watch accept hh>=24 in relative mode (the '+' prefix is already detected). Add a >24h relative-label test fixture.

title: CIQ field and FIT course are hard-wired to a single device (fenix7x); no other Garmin product is buildable or supported
evidence: manifest.xml declares only `<iq:product id="fenix7x"/>` and buildCiq.ts hardcodes `const DEVICE = 'fenix7x'`. The web Downloads text says 'Fenix 7X'. Any user on Edge/Forerunner/other fenix cannot install the field, yet the web app offers the course.fit/field download universally with no device gating.
recommendation: Add common cycling-capable products to the manifest products list (or prominently document the single-device limitation in the web download section). Treat fenix7x as one of several targets in buildCiq.ts.

title: Same rider inputs yield a different plan in CLI vs web because control points are derived differently (fixed VATTERN_CONTROLS vs controlsFromStops)
evidence: Web pipeline builds controls via controlsFromStops (Start + user stops + 'Mal' at route end); CLI cli.ts:165 uses soloControls which returns fixed VATTERN_CONTROLS for the non-solo path. Controls drive segmentation boundaries, the split/depot table, and the course-point set baked into course.fit/gpx, so the two front-ends produce divergent display segments, depots, and watch course points for identical inputs.
recommendation: Share one control-derivation function between cli and web (the soloControls/controlsFromStops duplication is already flagged) so outputs match for the same config, or explicitly document the intended divergence.

title: NaN coordinates/elevation from GPX flow unguarded into FIT semicircle and altitude encoding, producing a corrupt-but-valid course file
evidence: toSemicircles does `Math.round(deg * SEMICIRCLES_PER_DEGREE)`; with NaN lat/lon (a documented ingest outcome) the result is NaN, and altitude is written as raw `m.ele_start_m` (NaN when <ele> missing/non-numeric). These serialize as invalid field values into course.fit with no error, so the watch loads a structurally valid course with garbage positions/altitudes.
recommendation: Validate finiteness of lat/lon/ele at GPX ingest and additionally assert finiteness in buildCourseFit before encoding, throwing a clear error instead of emitting a poisoned FIT file.

title: buildCourseFit divides by totalDist and indexes microsegments[length-1] with no guard for empty/zero-length routes; Downloads click path has no try/catch
evidence: `const last = microsegments[microsegments.length - 1]` throws on an empty array, and a single-point route yields totalDist=0 so every course point shares timestamp BASE_MS. Empty/degenerate GPX reaches here unfiltered on the download path, which runs on the main thread in Downloads.tsx with no try/catch (onCourseFit/onCourse).
recommendation: Guard microsegments.length===0 and totalDist<=0 at the top of buildCourseFit (and buildCourseGpx) and surface a user error; wrap the Downloads.tsx builder calls in try/catch so a throw is not an uncaught main-thread error.

title: Zero logging/telemetry in packages/core and api: serverless weather function has no request id, no per-source success metric, silent catch{} blocks
evidence: grep for `console.` across packages/core/src and api returns nothing. Every upstream source wraps failures in `catch { return []; }` (fetchSmhi/fetchMetNorway/fetchOpenMeteoEnsemblePoint) with no log, so a persistent provider outage is invisible: the handler returns 200 with a thinner ensemble and operators get no signal. No request id or structured log on the Vercel function.
recommendation: Add structured logging on each per-source failure (source name + HTTP status) and a one-line per-request summary (points, date, sources-that-answered, cache disposition); consider returning reduced/sources info in a response header for client observability.

title: MET Norway User-Agent hardcoded to StickToThePlan/1.0 while every package.json is 0.1.0 (version drift; UA cannot track releases)
evidence: metNorwayHeaders returns `User-Agent: StickToThePlan/1.0 (${contact})` but root, core and web package.json all declare version 0.1.0. MET Norway uses the UA to contact operators about misbehaving clients; a static wrong version prevents correlating a problematic deploy, and there is no single source of truth for the app version.
recommendation: Source the version from package.json (build-time inject) so the User-Agent tracks the real release, or at least align the hardcoded string with the actual version.

title: Worker failure surfaces only a generic string; encodeWorkout's >50-step throw and pipeline errors reach the UI with no actionable context, and stale-run replies can mismatch
evidence: worker.onerror sets error to `event.message || 'Worker error'` then terminates and drops the worker. A module-load failure gives an opaque message; buildSteps throws a developer-facing string ('FIT workout would have N steps, exceeding the 50-step limit ... upstream error') that can surface verbatim to users. WorkerReply carries no run-id, so a reply from a stale run after recreate could be applied to a newer run.
recommendation: Tag each run with an id and ignore replies whose id does not match the latest run; map known internal errors (step cap, empty route) to user-friendly Swedish messages; log the raw error for diagnosis.

title: Workout 50-step throw is an implicit cross-module invariant with no boundary test; uploaded long routes can hit an uncaught throw on workout.fit download
evidence: encodeWorkout throws if steps>MAX_STEPS(50) with comment 'segmentation already enforces this upstream'. Default display maxSegs is 50 (segmentation.ts:482) and neutral-step dropping happens after counting, so the coupling is implicit and untested at the boundary; on a long/twisty uploaded route the workout.fit download (main thread, no try/catch) can throw uncaught.
recommendation: Make encodeWorkout defensively merge/truncate to 50 steps or fail gracefully in the UI rather than relying on an upstream invariant; add an end-to-end 50-step boundary test.

title: Course/route name baked into FIT and GPX is ASCII 'Vatternrundan' while the UI uses accented 'Vatternrundan' (encoding inconsistency across outputs)
evidence: fitCourse.ts COURSE_NAME and fitWorkout.ts WORKOUT_NAME are ASCII 'Vatternrundan', and course.ts writes `<name>Vatternrundan</name>` (ASCII), whereas the app header/UI uses the accented spelling. The watch course list shows the unaccented form, inconsistent with the rest of the product and with the GPX comment claiming diacritics are preserved.
recommendation: Standardize the course/workout name (use the accented form if the FIT string field and watch font support it), or document the ASCII choice as deliberate for device compatibility.

title: mapLimit worker loop has no per-task error isolation; a throw inside fn rejects Promise.all and orphans other in-flight fetches
evidence: mapLimit's worker does `results[i] = await fn(items[i])` with no try/catch. Current callers wrap fetch in try/catch so it is safe today, but the abstraction assumes fn never throws; a future caller or a synchronous throw (e.g. buildSmhiUrl on bad coords) would reject one worker, rejecting Promise.all and leaving other in-flight requests unhandled (no AbortController). A latent landmine given the codebase's unvalidated inputs.
recommendation: Document that fn must never reject, or capture per-item rejections into the results slot so one failure cannot abort the batch and orphan fetches.

title: No upstream fetch timeout means a single hanging provider holds the serverless function (and the concurrency pool) until the platform kills it
evidence: All fetch() calls (SMHI, MET Norway, Open-Meteo ensemble, batched forecast) pass no AbortSignal/timeout. gatherWindSamples awaits Promise.all of all four source groups, so the slowest hanging upstream pins the whole request for the function's max duration. vercel.json also sets no maxDuration, compounding the exposure.
recommendation: Add an AbortController with a per-request timeout (5-8s) to every upstream fetch and treat a timeout as a failed source (return []). Set maxDuration on the Vercel function.

title: Weather time handling is timezone-dependent: the same race date/time can produce different fields across hosts in different timezones
evidence: Per-track reviewers flagged the timezone misalignment and single-UTC-day window separately, but holistically this is a determinism-across-environments hazard: start_time is local wall clock, forecast hours are bucketed by ISO offset (truncateToHour assumes fixed offsets), so the field selected per segment depends on host TZ interpretation. The plan is not reproducible across machines in different timezones unless the offset is pinned.
recommendation: Normalize all weather time handling to one explicit timezone (Europe/Stockholm) at a single boundary, and add a cross-timezone determinism test (run with TZ=UTC vs TZ=America/Los_Angeles and assert identical output).

title: Validation is absent uniformly at EVERY external boundary; no shared runtime-schema layer, so each ingest/parse reinvents (and mostly omits) checks
evidence: Systemic pattern: GPX (gpx.ts), FIT (fit.ts), config (loadConfig/config), upstream weather JSON (openMeteo/smhi/metNorway), the API query (handler.ts), the web form (UploadForm.tsx), localStorage, and the worker message all accept untrusted input with `as` casts and no runtime schema. No validation library (zod/valibot) exists anywhere. This is the root cause behind the long tail of per-track NaN/crash findings rather than N independent bugs.
recommendation: Introduce one runtime-validation layer (e.g. zod) applied at each trust boundary: parsed GPX point, FIT power sample, RawConfig, each upstream weather payload, API query, web form, and worker PipelineInput. Collapses the NaN/crash long tail into one structural fix.

title: Example GPX (432KB) is inlined into the JS bundle, parsed twice per solve (main thread + worker), and copied into React state, multiplying memory/bundle cost
evidence: App.doFetch calls ingestGpxString on the main thread for weather sampling, and the worker pipeline (pipeline.ts:170) calls ingestGpxString again on the same text; defaultRoute.ts inlines a 432KB GPX via ?raw into the bundle and state. Combined with the unbounded GPX parser (no size cap, ~23x RSS amplification flagged elsewhere), the web path holds several route copies in memory at once.
recommendation: Parse the GPX once and pass microsegments (structured-clone-safe) to the worker instead of raw text, or sample weather points inside the worker; lazy-load the example GPX rather than inlining it in the main bundle.

title: @vercel/node declared-but-not-installed (api typecheck fails TS2307); the production entrypoint is the least pinned and least typechecked part of the repo
evidence: Per-track typecheck found api/weather.ts fails with @vercel/node not installed (TS2307), Vercel uses non-deterministic `npm install` (vercel.json), and there is no engines/.nvmrc Node pin. The one piece of code that runs in production (the serverless function) is the least pinned and least typecheck-covered, and its Vercel req/res contract is unvalidated.
recommendation: Add @vercel/node to devDependencies and pin it, pin Node via engines + .nvmrc, switch Vercel to `npm ci`, and include api/ in the CI typecheck so the production entrypoint is gated like the rest.

title: course.fit timestamps become non-monotonic and course points can collide when two controls snap to the same nearest microsegment
evidence: Course points are timestamped via tsAtDist(micro.cum_distance_m) where micro is the nearest microsegment to cp.km. Two controls closer than the microsegment spacing snap to the same micro, yielding identical timestamps/positions for distinct course points; on uploaded routes with nearby user stops this creates duplicate-distance course points the watch may reorder or de-duplicate, desyncing nameOfNextPoint from distanceToNextPoint.
recommendation: Detect controls that snap to the same microsegment and merge or nudge them; assert strictly increasing course-point distances before encoding.
